articles.title: What CareAround helps you do
articles.summary: Find community support, keep useful resources and plan what to do next.

sections.title: What can I do with CareAround?
paragraphs: CareAround SG helps you find community Places and Programmes/services in Discover. Sign in to save resources to My Directory, create private My Maps and share a view-only snapshot, and use Care Calendar for supported saved schedules and personal plans. You can also report app problems and follow replies in Inbox. If you manage a Place, the Guide can help you draft and review a Programme/service before you choose Create. Check eligibility, fees, availability, and registration with the provider.

sections.title: Places and Programmes/services
paragraphs: A Place is a physical resource such as a centre or service office. A Programme/service is an activity or support offering; it may be linked to a Place. Their schedules, audiences and access details can differ.

articles.title: Sign in and find your way around
articles.summary: Browse public information or sign in for your own saved resources and maps.

sections.title: Sign in to your existing account
paragraphs: Sign in to reach your own saved resources and maps. Use a sign-in method already linked to your account; staff and admins use this same sign-in form.
steps: Open Sign in and keep the Sign in tab selected.
For email sign-in, enter your Email address and Password, then select Sign in. If Google is already linked to your account, use the Google sign-in option instead.
Wait for the sign-in handoff to return you to the page you requested or to Dashboard. If the handoff offers Continue now, select it to continue.
Open My Directory from the dashboard navigation for your saved resources and My Maps. Use Discover to browse public listings.
notes: Discover and published Shared Maps can be browsed without signing in. Signing in does not give you permission to edit a public resource.
If a Google account needs linking, follow the message and sign in to the existing account first. Register creates an account; it is not an account-recovery step.

If your session has expired, sign in again. If the linked method fails or is unavailable, try another method already linked to the same account or submit a sign-in support report. Never put a password or verification code in chat or a report.

sections.title: Sign in with an already verified WhatsApp number
paragraphs: WhatsApp sign-in needs a number already verified in your CareAround profile and access to that WhatsApp account.
steps: On the Sign in tab, select Sign in with WhatsApp.
Enter the WhatsApp phone number already verified in your profile and confirm that you can use that WhatsApp account on this device.
Select Sign in with WhatsApp to start one attempt. If WhatsApp does not open, use Open WhatsApp when offered.
Send the prefilled message in WhatsApp, then return to CareAround while it checks the attempt. Keep the code within that sign-in flow.
When sign-in finishes, continue to your account. If the attempt expires or fails, use the offered Try again or Use Google/email option rather than starting several attempts at once.
notes: A number that is not verified on an existing account cannot establish access to that account. Sign in with its existing Google/email method first and verify the number in My Profile if needed.
Starting a new registration can create a separate account. If you meant to recover an existing account, stop and use a linked sign-in method or a support report instead.

sections.title: Browse without an account
paragraphs: You can browse public resources in Discover and open a published Shared Map without signing in. Sign in to save resources, create My Maps or copy someone else’s Shared Map into your own My Maps.

sections.title: Help with signing in
paragraphs: Try the sign-in method already linked to your account. If your session expired, sign in again. Avoid starting several WhatsApp verification attempts at once. You can report a sign-in problem here without signing in; keep the private recovery code to return to your report. Never send passwords or verification codes.

sections.title: Help with account access
paragraphs: The Guide cannot reset a password or change sign-in details. Open Sign in and use a sign-in method already available to your account. If you still cannot access it, submit a support report describing the sign-in problem. Never put a password or verification code in Guide chat or a report.

articles.title: Find a resource by name, category or location
articles.summary: Search public listings and use location as a starting point for checking support.

sections.title: Search Discover by name, service or category wording
paragraphs: Use Discover to find public Places and Programmes/services. You do not need an account for public browsing.
steps: Open Discover.
Enter a resource name, service, category wording, tag or address in the search field. For example, try a service term that a provider might use in its listing.
Use All to search both types, or choose Places or Programme/service. On a phone, open Filter and use Show to choose All, Places or Programmes & services only.
Open a matching result and read its location, description and any provider contact information. Confirm suitability and participation directly with the provider before relying on the result.
notes: Search matches recorded listing information; a missing result does not prove that a service or facility is unavailable.
If results are too narrow, shorten the wording, select All and turn off Saved only if it is enabled. Saved only restricts results to resources you have already saved.
Browsing or searching does not save a resource, book a seat or confirm eligibility. Use the related saving article when you want to keep a result in My Directory.

sections.title: Find resources near a postal code or your location
paragraphs: A location gives Discover a starting point for nearby browsing. You can combine it with a resource keyword; it is not an eligibility check.
steps: Open Discover. On a phone, open Filter to reach the location controls.

Enter a 6-digit Singapore postal code and wait for it to locate the address. Alternatively, select Locate me and allow the browser to use your location. If Home is available, select it to use your saved home postal code.
Choose All, Places or the Programme/service option and, if helpful, add a keyword such as a service name.
Open a result and check its actual address, service information and provider contact details before planning a visit.
notes: If the postal code cannot be located, check all six digits or try another valid nearby postal code. Discover looks up a completed postal code automatically; this control does not require a Find location button.
If browser location permission is denied or a location request times out, enter a postal code instead. Home is offered only when the account has a home postal code.
The search location changes this browsing starting point; it does not update your profile address or verify a provider’s current availability.

sections.title: Find a resource
paragraphs: Use resource search for a name, service, tag, or address. Open a result to check its current details. Discover also lets you browse Places and Programmes/services on the map. Search results are information, not a booking or a confirmation of eligibility.

sections.title: Find resources near you
paragraphs: Open Discover and enter a 6-digit Singapore postal code, or choose Locate Me and allow browser location access. If your account has a home postal code, you can use Home as the search location. Browse the resulting Places and Programmes/services and open a listing for its current details; location is a search aid, not a confirmation of eligibility or availability.

sections.title: Search for wheelchair-accessible resources
paragraphs: In Discover, try a keyword such as “wheelchair” or “step-free” with a postal code or Locate Me. Search can match wording in a listing’s name, description or tags, but I cannot verify a dedicated wheelchair-accessibility filter or that every provider records this information. Open a result and confirm the exact access needs, route and facilities directly with the provider before visiting. A missing keyword result does not prove a resource is inaccessible.

articles.title: Read resource details and check information with the provider
articles.summary: Check provider contact details, suitability, fees and participation before relying on a listing.

sections.title: Read a listing and contact its provider
paragraphs: Open a public listing to learn what the provider has supplied, then use an available provider channel to confirm anything needed for a visit or registration. Public browsing does not require sign-in.
steps: In Discover, search for the Place or Programme/service and open the matching result.
Check the listing’s name and location, then read its description and any schedule, audience, fees or availability information that is provided.
Look for the provider’s contact information. Use Website, Email, WhatsApp contact or an external link when shown; if a phone number is listed, use it through your phone.
Ask the provider to confirm current hours, fees, vacancies, eligibility and how to register or book. Tell them which Place or Programme/service you mean.
Keep any provider confirmation with your own planning information. Saving the listing in CareAround is a separate action and does not register you with the provider.
notes: Contact fields are optional. If no suitable channel is listed, do not infer that the provider can be reached through Guide chat; check another official provider channel or report the missing listing information.
A displayed availability count is not a confirmed seat or a live queue estimate. A directory fee is not a current price quote.

Website, email and WhatsApp links leave CareAround or open another app. Share personal details only with the intended provider through its appropriate channel; keep medical and identity details out of Guide chat.

If a listing is not visible, sign in and recheck Discover, then ask the provider or report its name. Profile criteria and active Place membership can affect visibility; the Guide cannot infer eligibility from an account role alone.

sections.title: Contact a resource provider
paragraphs: Find the Place or Programme/service in Discover and open its details. If the provider supplied contact information, the details can show a phone number, email, WhatsApp, website or external link. Use the available provider channel to confirm current hours, fees, places and registration. The Guide cannot message or register with the provider or book a seat for you, and I cannot verify an in-app provider chat or booking here.

sections.title: Current provider wait time
paragraphs: I cannot verify a Place or Programme/service’s current wait time from Guide chat. Open its listing in Discover and use any contact channel the provider has supplied to ask for a current estimate. A directory listing is not a live queue update.

sections.title: Confirm availability and fees
paragraphs: Some Programme/service details show an availability count when its manager enables that feature. Do not assume a listed service is free or that a remaining-seat count is live. A displayed count or fee is not a confirmed seat, price quote or provider booking. Resource details can change; contact the provider to confirm current availability, fees, eligibility and registration before relying on them.

sections.title: Programme and service eligibility
paragraphs: A Programme/service may have profile criteria, and a member-only one also requires an active membership at a linked Place. An account role alone does not bypass those checks. The Guide cannot confirm your eligibility for a particular listing from chat; open its current details if visible and confirm participation requirements with the provider. Eligibility is separate from booking or registration.

sections.title: A Programme or service is not visible
paragraphs: I cannot determine from chat why a particular Programme/service is not visible to you. Public visibility, audience scope, profile criteria and active linked-Place membership are separate checks. Sign in and recheck Discover; if the listing is still missing, ask the provider or report the listing name without sharing private profile details.

articles.title: Save and unsave a resource
articles.summary: Keep a resource for later and understand what saving or removing changes.

sections.title: Save a resource for later
paragraphs: Sign in to your own CareAround account before saving a Place or Programme/service.
steps: Open Discover, find the resource you want and open its details if you need to check it.
Select the heart labelled Save to My Directory on that resource.
Wait for the save request to finish. A saved heart is filled; its label changes to Remove from My Directory.
Open My Directory → Saved resources and check that the intended resource is listed.
notes: A Place and each linked Programme/service are saved separately. Save the particular listing you want to keep.
Saving keeps a personal bookmark. It does not register you, join a Place, establish eligibility, grant editing rights or add the resource to a map.

If no heart is available, check that you are signed in. If the control is busy or saved resources cannot be loaded, wait or retry loading before trying again. A brief heart change is not enough to confirm a failed request succeeded.
If the item is missing from Saved resources, clear the saved-list search and filters and check the exact listing. For current availability, contact the provider.

sections.title: Remove one item from your saved list
paragraphs: Use these steps to remove your own bookmark, rather than delete a public listing or remove a resource from a map. You must be signed in.
steps: Open My Directory → Saved resources and find the item you want to remove.
Select Remove on that saved-resource card.
Read the confirmation, including any warning about My Maps or the Programme/service’s Care Calendar schedule source.
If you still want to unsave it, select Remove from My Directory. Choose Cancel to keep it.
Wait for the request to finish and check that the item is no longer in your saved list.
notes: The public resource remains available to other people. If it was added to one of your maps, it stays in that map; map membership is a separate choice.
You can also toggle a saved heart on the resource itself. Use the Saved resources removal workflow when you need to review the map/calendar warnings first.
Unsaving a Programme/service can remove its saved schedule source from Care Calendar. Check your plans before confirming.
If map use cannot be checked or removal reports an error, retry the displayed loading action and recheck the list. Do not assume the removal finished.

sections.title: Remove several saved resources not used in your maps
paragraphs: Bulk removal operates on your saved list and protects resources used in your My Maps. Sign in and wait for the app to check map use.
steps: Open My Directory → Saved resources.
Under My Map use, choose Not used in My Maps to review the unused items.
Select Select to remove, then tick the items you want to unsave. Select all shown selects the visible unused items; Clear selection removes the ticks.
Select Remove followed by the selected count, then read the confirmation and its Care Calendar warning for any Programme/service.
Confirm Remove only when you have reviewed the selection, or choose Cancel to leave your saved list unchanged.
Read the result and check your saved list. Any items now used in My Maps are kept rather than bulk removed.
notes: Used in My Maps is a separate filter for inspecting resources your maps use. Those items cannot be selected for bulk removal.
If map use cannot be checked, bulk removal pauses. Use Retry and wait for the check to finish; do not work around the protection.
Bulk removal does not delete public resources. Unsaving selected Programmes/services can remove their saved schedule sources from Care Calendar.

sections.title: Save resources
paragraphs: Use the heart on a resource to save it to My Directory. You must be signed in to save. Saving an Offering is not registration for its programme or service.

sections.title: Remove saved resources safely
paragraphs: In My Directory, filter saved resources by Used in My Maps or Not used in My Maps. Select unused resources and review the removal confirmation. Bulk removal protects resources used in your maps. Unsaving an Offering can remove its saved schedule source from Care Calendar; check that warning before confirming.

sections.title: Remove a saved resource from My Directory
paragraphs: If you mean removing a Place or Offering from your own saved list, open My Directory and choose its Unsave or Remove saved control. This changes your saved list; it does not delete the public listing or remove that resource from a My Map. Review any confirmation before bulk removal.

sections.title: Saving a resource and your identity
paragraphs: Using the heart saves the Place or Programme/service to your own My Directory. That Save action does not send your name or profile details to the provider, notify the provider that you saved the listing, register you, or link you as a Place member. My Directory is not a public saver list. Joining a Place through its membership link is separate: authorised Place managers can see membership details, including names. Contacting a provider or publishing a Shared Map is also separate from saving. The Guide cannot identify who saved a provider’s listing or check another person’s saved list.

sections.title: Save a Place separately from its Programmes
paragraphs: A Place and its linked Programmes/services are separate resources. You can save the Place without saving each Programme/service; use the heart on any Programme/service you also want in My Directory. Saving either one does not register you for a Programme/service or give you permission to edit its listing.

sections.title: Saving does not grant eligibility
paragraphs: Saving a Programme/service to My Directory is a personal bookmark. It does not satisfy profile criteria, create Place membership, grant access to a restricted listing, or register you with the provider. Check the listing’s current details and ask the provider about participation.

sections.title: A saved resource is missing or unavailable
paragraphs: I cannot tell why a particular saved resource is missing or unavailable from a general question. Check My Directory for your saved item. If its listing has changed or disappeared, report the resource and what you expected to see. For current service availability or registration, confirm directly with the provider.

articles.title: Understand Saved Resources, My Maps, My Places and managed resources
articles.summary: Choose the personal directory section you need and understand separate editing rights.

sections.title: Saved resources and managed resources
paragraphs: Saving a Place or Programme/service with its heart adds it to My Directory for your own use. Saving does not itself give you permission to edit or manage that resource, and saving a Programme/service does not register or book you for it. You may have separate management rights; check Manage My Resources in the dashboard for Places and Programmes/services assigned to your account.

sections.title: Who can see saved resources
paragraphs: My Directory loads the resources saved by your signed-in account; it is not a public list of everything you saved. A staff role alone does not grant another person a view of your whole saved list through My Directory or Guide chat. Publishing a Shared Map makes its selected snapshot available through that link, not your whole saved list. Review the shared snapshot before giving anyone its link.

sections.title: Export all of My Directory
paragraphs: I cannot verify a one-click export of every saved resource in My Directory. Export Map Assets belongs to an individual My Map and exports that map’s resource workbook, not your whole saved list. If you need a particular map’s list, open that owned map in My Directory and use Export Map Assets. Review the file before sharing it, especially if your map contains private planning places.

sections.title: Where to find listings assigned to you
paragraphs: Sign in and open the dashboard, then choose Manage My Resources when that control is available to your account. Choose Places, Offerings or Groups to review the listings you can manage. My Directory is a separate page for resources you saved for your own use.

If Manage My Resources is missing, this account may not currently have resource-management access. Saving a listing or belonging to an organisation does not grant editing permission. Check the exact listing’s current controls or ask the responsible Owner or administrator to review your assignment; the Guide cannot grant access.

articles.title: Create a My Map
articles.summary: Sign in and open My Directory → My Maps. You can choose saved resources or find more resources within the creation dialog.

sections.title: Create your map
paragraphs: Sign in and open My Directory → My Maps. You can choose saved resources or find more resources within the creation dialog.
steps: Choose Create map and enter a map name.
Select the saved resources you want in this map. To search other available resources, use Search saved and all resources.
For an available unsaved result, choose Save and add; review the selected resources.
Choose Create map to finish.
Wait for the new map to open, then check its name and resource list. If creation reports an error, check My Maps before trying to create it again.
notes: A map needs a name and at least one selected resource before Create map is available.
Save and add saves that resource to My Directory immediately. Cancelling map creation does not undo that save. Creating or updating the map is a separate action.
A selected Programme/service can also select its linked Place. Review the resulting collection.

sections.title: Create and manage My Maps
paragraphs: If your signed-in account can use My Directory, open it and choose My Maps to create or open a map. The Create/Manage Resources controls let you search for resources and add them to that map. Use the map menu for Map Studio. Changes to your private map do not silently update an already published Shared Map.

articles.title: Add or remove resources in an existing map
articles.summary: Use the map’s resource selection to change this one map.

sections.title: Change this map’s collection
paragraphs: Saving a Place or Programme/service adds it to My Directory. You choose separately whether to add it to a particular My Map. Use the map’s resource selection to change this one map.
steps: Open a My Map you own and choose Manage resources.
Select resources to include and untick resources to leave out. Use the combined search and Save and add for another available listing if needed.
Review the selection and choose Update map.
Wait for the selection dialog to close, then check this map’s resource list. If an error remains, review the current selection before retrying.
notes: Save and add saves immediately to My Directory; Update map applies the selected map membership.
Removing a resource from this map does not delete its public listing or automatically unsave it. Pin visibility is a separate presentation control.
A failed update can leave some additions or removals already applied. Check this map’s current collection before retrying; the error is not proof that nothing changed.

sections.title: Saved resources and map membership
paragraphs: Saving a resource adds it to My Directory. You choose separately whether to add it to a particular My Map. If a saved Programme/service is missing from a map, open My Directory → My Maps, choose that map and use its resource controls to add the Programme/service. Removing it from a map does not automatically unsave it from My Directory.

sections.title: Remove a resource from one My Map
paragraphs: If you mean removing a resource from one of your My Maps, open that map and use its resource controls. This changes that map’s membership; it does not unsave the resource from My Directory or delete the public listing. If you mean hiding its pin in a Map Studio view instead, that is a presentation change and the resource card remains available, so check which result you want before editing.

articles.title: Add a missing location as a Personal place on your map
articles.summary: Add a private planning location that is missing from the public directory.

sections.title: Add the missing location to your own map
paragraphs: Yes—you can add a missing location as a Personal place. You must be signed in and use a map you own.
steps: Open My Directory → My Maps and open your map.
Select + Personal place.
Select Choose map location, then click or tap the spot on your map.
Enter the place’s name and category.
Enter its address or postal code in the lookup and select Find location to verify it.
Review the returned location and details, then select Save.
notes: On a phone, select Open map controls, then Personal place.
For a genuine point without a postal address, select This point has no postal address instead. Do not guess a postal code from a nearby building.
The place is kept in My Places and can be reused on your other maps. It remains private: it does not enter Discover or public Shared Maps, but can appear in your own printed/exported maps.
If location verification fails, check the address or six-digit Singapore postal code and try again. A failed save is not confirmation that the place was added.
To submit a public directory listing instead, use the authorised public Place workflow; a Personal place is for your own planning.

articles.title: Verify a Personal place address or use a genuine point without an address
articles.summary: An addressed Personal place needs a verified Singapore address and six-digit postal code. Find location fills the returned address and coordinates; check that they describe the intended place.

sections.title: Verify an addressed place or choose a genuine map-only point
paragraphs: An addressed Personal place needs a verified Singapore address and six-digit postal code. Find location fills the returned address and coordinates; check that they describe the intended place.

Sign in to create or edit your own Personal places. Open My Directory → My Places to edit a place you own, or use the Personal place editor on a My Map you own. Guests can read these instructions but cannot save Personal places.
steps: In the Personal place editor, enter the address or postal code in the location lookup.
Select Find location and review the returned address, postal code and location.
If you change the address, postal code or coordinates afterward, verify the location again before saving.
Use This point has no postal address only for a genuine coordinate-only planning point, then review its map location before Save.
Select Save after checking the name, category and location. When saving succeeds, the editor closes and My Places or the owned map you are editing shows the saved location.
notes: An addressed place cannot be saved while location verification is incomplete. If verification is temporarily unavailable, retry later; do not convert an addressed building into a map-only point to bypass verification.
A genuine map-only point has no address or postal code.
Personal places stay private: saving does not add them to Discover or public Shared Maps. Your owner map exports can include these places, so review downloaded files before sharing them.

articles.title: Reuse, edit, detach or delete a Personal place
articles.summary: Keep reusable private places and check whether an action affects one map or every linked map.

sections.title: Reuse a place and distinguish removal from deletion
steps: Open your own map and choose + Personal place.
Search My Places, select the place or places to reuse, then choose Add to this map.
To edit a place, open My Directory → My Places and use Edit on that place. Review its location before saving.
Read the confirmation carefully before deleting from My Places: Delete everywhere removes the place from My Places and its linked maps.
notes: Removing a Personal place from one map leaves it in My Places. Deleting it from My Places has the wider effect described in the confirmation.

sections.title: My Places
paragraphs: My Places in My Directory are private planning locations you can reuse across your own maps. Open My Places and choose Add personal place to create one. Removing a personal place from one map leaves it in My Places; deleting it from My Places removes it from every linked map. Saving a private planning location does not make it a public directory Place or assign it to you to manage.

sections.title: Edit a private My Place address
paragraphs: For a personal place you own, open My Directory → My Places and choose Edit on that place. In the editor, update its postal code and address, check the location, then save. The server checks ownership when saving. This changes your private planning place, not a public directory Place; the Guide cannot edit it from chat.

sections.title: Remove a Personal place from this map only
paragraphs: Sign in and open a map you own. A Personal place’s Remove action takes effect immediately; it does not show the separate public-resource removal confirmation.
steps: Open the map containing the Personal place. On a phone, select Open map controls to reach the map’s editing controls.
Select Edit content → Remove resources to show removal controls on the map’s resource cards.
Find the intended Personal place card and check its name. Select its Remove control, labelled Remove from map for accessibility.
Wait for Personal place removed from your map, then check that the card is no longer in this map.
Open My Directory → My Places if you want to reuse it. Removing it from one map leaves the place there and on any other maps that use it.
notes: This is separate from Hide pin, which only changes presentation, and Delete everywhere in My Places, which removes the place more widely.
If removal or the map refresh fails, reopen the map and check its current collection before retrying. Do not use Delete everywhere as a workaround for a map-only removal.

sections.title: Delete a Personal place from My Places and its maps
paragraphs: Use deletion only when you want to remove the Personal place from My Places and every map linked to it. To remove it from one map, use that map’s Remove control instead.
steps: Open My Directory → My Places and find the Personal place you intend to delete.
Select that card’s trash control, labelled Delete everywhere.
Read Delete personal place. Check the place name and the number of maps in the confirmation, or the permanent-removal message when it is on no maps.
Select Delete everywhere in the confirmation to proceed, or Cancel to keep the place.
Wait for the card to disappear from My Places. Reopen any affected maps to check the updated collection.
notes: Deleting a Personal place does not delete a public directory listing; Personal places are your own private planning records.
If deletion reports an error, check My Places and the affected maps before retrying. Do not assume an error means the place was kept.

articles.title: Open Map Studio and keep a saved view on desktop or mobile
articles.summary: Select a map presentation and check that its changes have saved.

sections.title: Choose a view and check its save status
paragraphs: A named Map Studio view is a presentation of the same map, rather than another resource collection. On desktop, use the Map Studio panel on your map. On a phone, open the map menu and choose Map Studio.
steps: Open a map you own. On desktop, use its Map Studio panel; on a phone, select Open map controls → Map Studio.
Use the View selector to choose a saved view. To start another view, select New view, enter New view name, and select Create view. To copy the selected view’s presentation instead, select Duplicate.
Use Edit layout for the view’s design controls, or Edit content for supported content-editing modes. Make the intended changes to the selected view.
Wait for All changes saved in Map Studio. If saving fails, use Retry save when offered and check the result before leaving or sharing the view.
notes: The released Studio uses saving-status feedback. Discard abandons unsaved design changes. Do not assume closing a panel means a failed save succeeded.
A saved Studio view does not update a published Shared Map. Use the sharing controls to publish or update the intended view separately.
New view needs a non-empty name before Create view is available. Duplicate makes another presentation of the same map; it does not duplicate the resource collection into a new My Map.

sections.title: Map Studio views
paragraphs: Map Studio saves a presentation of a My Map. Saving or changing a Studio view does not by itself refresh the published Shared Map or its embedded presentation. Select the saved view when explicitly publishing or updating the shared snapshot, then preview the embedded result.

articles.title: Print or export your own map
articles.summary: Choose the right visual map, notes or resource-list download.

sections.title: Save a visual map as PNG or PDF, then print it
paragraphs: Sign in and open a map you own. Export View creates a visual copy; it is separate from the Map Notes PDF and the resource workbook.
steps: Open My Directory → My Maps and open your map.
If you use Map Studio, select the view you want to export and wait for its saved-status confirmation.
Select Export View in the map toolbar. On a phone, open the map menu to find Export View.
Review the export preview, including the title, visible resources, private planning content and the map’s position and zoom.
Wait for Map ready to download. Select Save PNG for an image or Save PDF for the visual PDF.
Open the downloaded file and check the map and its pages before sharing it. To print, use the Print control in the PDF viewer.
notes: Some layouts show separate Save Map PNG and Save Resource PNG controls. Choose the page you need; the resource-only image is not a map image.
If Map download is not ready is shown, use Retry map preparation and wait. If Studio changes could not be saved, return to the map, resolve the save error and reopen Export View.

Owner exports can contain Personal places and other private planning content. Public Shared Map exclusions are not a promise that your own file contains only public content; inspect the file before giving it to anyone.
The download is a snapshot. Recheck important provider contacts, dates, availability and eligibility before relying on or sharing an older copy.
Exporting does not publish or update a Shared Map. Use Share separately for its public version.

sections.title: Download notes or an Excel resource list
paragraphs: Use your owned map’s separate downloads when you need notes or a resource list rather than a picture of the map.
steps: Sign in, open My Directory → My Maps and open the map you own.
For the notes ledger, select Download Map Notes. For an Excel resource workbook, select Export Map Assets. On a phone, find these controls in the map menu.
Wait for the PDF or Excel preparation to finish. If exporting the resource workbook, allow pending Map Studio changes to save first.
Open the downloaded PDF or workbook and check its contents, including any Personal places, before sharing or printing it.
If you need a visual map instead, return to the map and select Export View, then choose Save PNG or Save PDF.
notes: Export Map Assets creates an Excel workbook with a Summary and Map Assets sheet. Private map notes are not included in that workbook; review the remaining resource and Personal place details before sharing.
Download Map Notes produces the notes/ledger PDF, not the visual-map PDF. Save PDF inside Export View is the visual version.
If preparation fails, read the error and retry the same download once the map and any Studio save have finished. A preparation message does not mean the file was downloaded.
Downloads are copies of the current map content, not live updates or programme registrations.

sections.title: My Map downloads
paragraphs: An owned My Map has separate downloads for different purposes: Download Map Notes creates a PDF ledger, and Export Map Assets creates a resource workbook. Use the map image or Export View when you need a visual map. A downloaded file is a snapshot; recheck important provider details before sharing it.

articles.title: Publish, update or stop sharing a map
articles.summary: Publish the intended version and review what recipients can see.

sections.title: Publish the intended saved view
paragraphs: A Shared Map keeps the version explicitly published through Share. Editing the private map or saving its Studio presentation does not automatically change that snapshot.
steps: Open your own map and select the Studio view you intend to share.
Check that the design has saved, then open Share.
Review the notes and annotation settings intended for recipients.
Choose Publish share link for a first publication, or Update shared link to replace the published snapshot.

After publication or update completes, use Copy link and open that link in another browser tab to inspect the public version before sending it. If the design has newer unpublished changes, Copy existing link copies the earlier published version.
To stop sharing, reopen Share and select Unpublish. Wait for the private-map status before assuming the shared version is no longer available.
notes: Copying the existing link alone does not update its content.
Personal places are excluded from public Shared Maps. Owner prints and exports can include private planning content; check files separately.
An embedded presentation uses its published snapshot and omits resource-note rows. Preview the actual embed separately.
Unpublish starts from that button without an additional confirmation dialog. If publishing, updating or unpublishing reports an error, reopen Share and check its current status before retrying.

sections.title: Share a map
paragraphs: Open your own map and review its sharing controls. A Shared Map is a view-only snapshot; update the shared version explicitly after changing your private map. Review what will be visible before sharing the link. You can stop sharing from the same controls.

sections.title: Saving versus publishing a resource on a Shared Map
paragraphs: Saving a Place or Programme/service adds it to your My Directory, not automatically to any My Map or Shared Map. Add that saved resource to the particular My Map you own. A published Shared Map is a separate snapshot: explicitly update the shared version and preview it before visitors can see the changed map. The Guide cannot add or publish it for you.

sections.title: Who opened a Shared Map
paragraphs: The Guide cannot show who opened a Shared Map or identify viewers from chat. The reviewed My Map sharing controls let you inspect and update the published snapshot and stop sharing; I cannot verify an owner-facing viewer list or view-count report there. Review the content and link before sharing, and use Help to describe any reporting need without including other people’s details.

sections.title: Embed a Shared Map on a website
paragraphs: From the Share controls of a published My Map, add an approved website, enable Website Embed, save the embed settings, and copy the embed code. The embedded presentation uses the published snapshot rather than unsaved map changes. Preview it and review guest-visible content before placing it on a website.

sections.title: Personal places and sharing
paragraphs: Personal places are excluded from a published Shared Map. Your owner map and its resource-ledger downloads can include them, so review an export before sharing it with anyone. A personal place is not a public directory Place.

articles.title: Add private map notes and review shared notes
articles.summary: Write resource notes and decide which individual notes are intended for sharing.

sections.title: Write and check a private resource note
paragraphs: Add a resource note to a My Map you own. You must be signed in, and the map needs at least one resource to choose. New notes have Share this note turned off.
steps: Open My Directory → My Maps and choose your own map.
Select Map notes, then choose the resource you want to write about.
Enter your note. If the existing note is shown as a preview, select Edit first. Use Add another note when you want a separate note for the same resource.
Keep Share this note off for private planning information. Use Preview if you want to check how the text will read.
Use Back to map notes or Close map notes to leave the editor and start saving the changes. Reopen the resource’s note and check that the saved text is present before relying on it.
notes: Typing a note alone is not proof that it has saved. If a save error is shown, use Save notes when offered and check again; a failed save must not be treated as persisted information.
Remove note deletes that note from your map when its save succeeds. It does not remove the resource from My Directory or delete a public listing.
Your private note is separate from the public provider description. Keep passwords, identity numbers, medical records and sensitive case details out of map notes.

sections.title: Choose a note for a published Shared Map
paragraphs: Choose sharing separately for each resource note. Marking a note for sharing does not itself update an existing public link.
steps: Open your own My Map → Map notes and choose the resource.
Review the note’s entire text and turn on Share this note only if it is intended for anyone who can open the shared link. Leave other notes switched off.
Check that the note and its sharing choice save successfully. If an error appears, use Save notes when offered before continuing.
Close the note editor and open Share. Choose Publish share link for a map you have not shared, or Update shared link for an existing published map.
Open the published Shared Map and check the recipient view before sending its link.
notes: Turning Share this note off changes the owner’s saved choice; update the shared link again to remove that note from the published snapshot. Visitors continue to see the last published version until you update or unpublish it.

The website embed omits resource-note rows, including notes marked for sharing. Annotation overlays use separate controls; check the actual embedded view rather than assuming it matches the regular Shared Map page.
Publishing is a separate explicit action. A shared note is intended for link recipients, and the shared link can be forwarded.

sections.title: Add a note to a My Map resource
paragraphs: Open My Directory → My Maps and choose a map you own. Open Map Notes, choose the resource, then enter your note and check that it saves. Each note has its own Share this note switch, which is off by default. Review and explicitly update a published Shared Map before relying on a shared note there. The website embed omits resource notes from its resource rows.

sections.title: My Map note and annotation sharing
paragraphs: Resource notes on your My Map stay private unless you enable Share this note for each note. An explicitly published or updated Shared Map snapshot includes the notes marked for sharing. Print annotations have a separate share setting, and a selected Map Studio view can hide annotations in an embedded presentation. Preview the published or embedded view before sharing its link.

articles.title: Add annotations and review their sharing behaviour
articles.summary: Understand the separate sharing rules for annotations, note rows and embeds.

sections.title: Draw and save an annotation on your own map
paragraphs: Use annotations to draw a line, box, circle or boundary on a My Map you own. Sign in and use a desktop with a mouse or another fine pointer; the current editor is not available for ordinary phone touch input.
steps: Open My Directory → My Maps and choose your own map.
Choose Edit content → Annotations and wait for the annotation editor to be ready.
Choose Draw line, Draw box, Draw circle or Draw boundary.

For a line, click its start and end points. For a box, click opposite corners. For a circle, click its centre and outer edge. For a boundary, click at least three points, then select Done drawing or press Enter.

Choose Select or adjust and select the annotation to adjust its handles or appearance. You can use Move annotation or Rotate annotation, or add an optional Note inside shape. Click outside the text field to finish that text edit.
Wait until the toolbar says Saved, then close the annotation editor.
notes: New annotations are private unless you mark them for sharing and explicitly publish or update the shared snapshot. Drawing does not create a Personal place or a public resource listing.
Use Undo to reverse a completed change. Select an annotation and use Delete annotation to remove it; wait for Saved again.

If Annotations is unavailable, check that this is your own map, that the annotation data has loaded and that you are using a suitable desktop pointer. Normal phone/touch creation is not currently offered.

Pending, Saving... or Save failed is not confirmation of a saved annotation. Closing starts a save attempt but does not guarantee success. If Save failed persists, keep the editor open and resolve the connection problem or submit a support report before relying on or publishing the drawing.

sections.title: Choose which saved annotations become public
paragraphs: Annotation sharing is separate from resource-note sharing. Only use text and drawings intended for public link recipients.
steps: Open the annotation editor on your own map, select the annotation and review its text and location.
Turn on Share this annotation for each item you intend to publish; leave private items switched off. Wait for Saved.

Open Share. If this map already has a shared link, review Include annotations and its count. Changing this control selects all saved annotations or none; leaving it unchanged keeps your individual choices.
Select Publish share link for a new public snapshot or Update shared link for an existing one.
Preview the actual published or embedded view that you intend to send before sharing its link.
notes: Owner edits and sharing switches do not automatically refresh an existing published snapshot. Update the shared link after changing which annotations should be public.
Published website embeds can display shared annotations read-only, but a selected Map Studio presentation can hide them. Do not assume every ordinary Shared Map screen displays the same overlay.

Resource notes are omitted from website-embed resource rows. A Personal place’s privacy rules are separate from annotation sharing, so do not draw or label private locations that you do not want public recipients to see.

sections.title: Review annotations before sharing
paragraphs: Resource notes and print annotations have separate sharing controls. In Share, review Include annotations before publishing or updating the snapshot. The embedded result should be previewed because its selected presentation can hide annotation overlays.
notes: Use only information intended for recipients. Do not put identity numbers, medical records or sensitive case details into shared drawings or labels.
A personal place’s privacy rule is separate from an annotation’s sharing setting.

sections.title: Notes in an embedded Shared Map
paragraphs: The embedded Shared Map response omits My Map resource notes from its resource rows, including notes marked for sharing. Print annotations are a separate control: only annotations included in the published embed snapshot can appear as an overlay. Preview the actual embed before sharing it; the regular Shared Map page has different note controls.

articles.title: Understand missing pins, list-only resources, filters and map framing
articles.summary: Check list-only resources, pin visibility and Detailed display without assuming deletion.

sections.title: A listed resource may have no usable pin
paragraphs: A resource that remains in the map’s list is not necessarily missing from the collection. List-only resources can remain in the directory without a map position.
steps: Check whether the resource appears in this map’s list; map membership is separate from saving it in My Directory.
Look for List only or an unavailable status, and open the current resource details when offered.

If you own this map, select the intended View in Map Studio and open Edit layout; on a phone, select Open map controls → Edit layout. Check Map pins → Show and Resource categories; if needed, show the pins and tick the intended group and category. Wait for All changes saved after making changes, then move or zoom the map to inspect the intended area.
If the location is missing or incorrect, contact the listing maintainer or report the problem. Do not create duplicate public listings or guess a postal code as a workaround.
notes: Hiding a pin changes the presentation; it does not remove the resource card or delete the public listing.

Changing these presentation settings cannot supply missing coordinates to a List only resource. A public Shared Map keeps its last published view; ask its owner about a display change rather than assuming you can edit it.

sections.title: Check Detailed map display
paragraphs: In Discover, open Map settings to choose Standard or Detailed. Detailed uses the overview map from zoom 14 up to, but not including, zoom 16; zoom 16 or above shows native detail with block numbers where the surface is available. A loading bar appears while Detailed prepares, and you can keep using the map. Discover and your editable My Map use 0.5 steps for the zoom buttons and keyboard; trackpad and pinch zoom stay smooth. My Map and its owner Print View keep native detail from zoom 15. Shared, embedded, and print map controls keep their existing behavior. If the view looks wrong, report the page and zoom level.

sections.title: Show a pin hidden in your map view
paragraphs: Use this when a mapped resource remains in your own map’s collection but its pin was hidden in the selected Studio view. A List only resource without usable coordinates cannot gain a pin through this control.
steps: Open your map and use Map Studio’s View selector to choose the presentation you are checking.
Select Edit content → Hide map pins. On a phone, select Open map controls first to reach Edit content.
Find the intended mapped Place card and select Show pin when offered. Hide pin is the opposite action.
Wait for All changes saved in Map Studio, then move or zoom the map to inspect that location.
Select Edit content → Hide map pins again when you want to leave that editing mode.
notes: This changes the selected view’s pin presentation. It does not add a resource to the map, fix its coordinates, or change the public listing.
Other presentation settings can still hide that pin. Check Map pins and Resource categories under Edit layout if Show pin alone does not reveal it.
If the resource is unavailable or List only, inspect the current listing details when offered and report the location problem rather than guessing a postal code.

sections.title: Check hidden map pins and category filters
paragraphs: The selected Studio view can hide all map pins or particular resource categories. Check these display choices separately from the map’s collection.
steps: Open a map you own and select the intended View in Map Studio.
Select Edit layout. On a phone, select Open map controls → Edit layout.
Under Map pins, select Show if the pins are hidden.
Open Resource categories when available. Tick the intended group, then tick the category within it. A category cannot be turned on while its parent group is hidden.
Wait for All changes saved, then move or zoom the map to inspect the intended area. Check individual Show pin controls if one mapped Place remains hidden.
notes: These presentation choices do not delete public resources or unsave resources from My Directory. They also cannot supply a missing map location.
A public Shared Map keeps its last published view. To change that public presentation, save your own view and explicitly update the shared link separately.

articles.title: Export Map Assets and understand the workbook
articles.summary: Download the resource workbook for one owned map and review it before forwarding.

sections.title: Download and review the Excel workbook
paragraphs: Export Map Assets downloads an Excel workbook for one My Map you own. Sign in and open that map; this is not an export of your entire My Directory.
steps: Open My Directory → My Maps and choose the map you want to export.
Review the resources included by the selected Map Studio view before exporting. If you need a different collection, change the view’s resource selections first and let those changes save.
Select Export Map Assets in the map controls. On a phone, open the map’s controls menu to find it.
Wait while the workbook is prepared, then find the downloaded .xlsx file using your browser’s downloads.
Open the workbook and check both Summary and Map Assets. Review names, categories, addresses, postal codes, types and short descriptions before forwarding the file.
notes: The workbook can include your Personal places and map short descriptions. Private resource notes are not included, but that does not make the whole owner export suitable for public sharing.

Map Studio resource selections affect the exported collection. The map’s keyword search is not used to narrow this workbook, and hiding a pin is not a reliable way to remove that resource from the file. Check the actual workbook.
The file is a snapshot. Download a new workbook after relevant map or listing changes; sending it does not publish a Shared Map or give recipients editing permission.

If Excel download failed is shown, check that pending map changes have saved and retry Export Map Assets. If no file is visible after a successful preparation, check the browser’s download location or download prompt.

sections.title: Which resource workbook was downloaded?
paragraphs: Which download do you mean? If it is Export Map Assets from an owned My Map, the downloaded resource workbook is a snapshot and does not refresh when listings or the map change. Generate a new download when you need the map’s current resource list, and review provider details and private planning places before sharing it. A workbook from another screen has a different scope; tell me that screen or download label so I can give the matching steps. The Guide cannot re-export or upload a file for you.

sections.title: Share a private My Map workbook
paragraphs: For an owned My Map, Export Map Assets creates a workbook for that map, not your whole My Directory. Your owner map export can include private planning places, so review the workbook before sharing it with anyone. Sending the file is a separate choice from publishing a Shared Map snapshot, and the file will not track later map changes.

articles.title: View or copy a Shared Map
articles.summary: Use a view-only snapshot or make an editable private copy when offered.

sections.title: Open a published Shared Map
paragraphs: A published ordinary Shared Map is a view-only snapshot you can open without signing in. You need its current working share link.
steps: Open the published Shared Map link provided by its owner.
Check the map name and browse its map and resource list. Open a resource to read its supplied details.
If you want a print-friendly layout, choose Print-friendly view. On a phone, open the shared map controls menu to find this option.
Confirm time-sensitive details with the resource provider before using them for a visit or registration.
notes: You are viewing the version the owner last published. Later private edits appear only after the owner updates the shared link.
The shared page does not let you add to or edit the owner’s original My Map. Viewing it does not save its resources in your My Directory.
If the link no longer opens, ask the owner for a working published link. It may have been unpublished; signing in does not restore an unavailable snapshot.

sections.title: Make your own private copy when offered
paragraphs: Copy to My Maps creates a separate private map from the published snapshot. You must be signed in with access to My Maps, be a visitor rather than its owner and have this copy option available.
steps: Open the ordinary Shared Map link and review the snapshot you want to copy.
If you are signed out, use Sign in and return to the shared page after signing in to your existing account.
Select Copy to My Maps when it is offered. On a phone, open the shared map controls menu to find it.
Wait for the copy to open as your own My Map. Check its resources and any copied shared notes.
Edit your own copy using its map controls. Keep it private, or deliberately use Share when you later want to publish your version.
notes: Your copy does not change the owner’s original and does not automatically follow later updates to that original. It contains the public snapshot rather than the owner’s private map data.
Copied shared resource notes start private in your new map. Review your own sharing choices before publishing your copy.
Copying a map does not give you permission to edit the providers’ public resource listings.

Copy to My Maps is not offered for every shared-map type: governed shared maps do not support this workflow, and owners already have their original map. If the button is absent, use the view-only page or open the original map you already own. If copying reports an error, check your sign-in and retry only after the problem is resolved.

sections.title: Copy a Shared Map
paragraphs: Only the owner can add a saved resource to the original private My Map. Sharing publishes a view-only snapshot; it does not let a visitor add a Place to your original. When Copy to My Maps is available, a signed-in visitor can make a separate private map from the snapshot and edit their copy; it does not change the original map.

articles.title: Download a town map versus exporting your own My Map
articles.summary: Find town-map downloads and distinguish them from your own map exports.

sections.title: Download a high-detail town map file
paragraphs: High-Detail Town Maps provides prepared town-map files in PNG and PDF formats. Sign in with access to My Directory; these downloads are separate from the contents of your own My Maps.
steps: Open High-Detail Town Maps in the dashboard navigation.
Use Search town maps to enter a town name or map code, then find the matching town card.
Check the town and covered areas, preview and PNG/PDF file sizes. Use Wi-Fi if a large download would use too much mobile data.
Select Download PNG for an image or Download PDF for a PDF file, then wait for the browser to start the download.
Check your browser’s downloads and open the file to confirm that you chose the intended town and format.
notes: These are prepared town-map files; they do not add your saved resources, Personal places or private map notes. Downloading one does not create or change a My Map.
For your own mapped resources and layout, open an owned My Map and use Export View or its map export controls. Export Map Assets produces a resource workbook rather than this town-map PNG/PDF.

If search finds no maps, shorten the town name or use Clear search. If the catalogue cannot load, use Try again. If a download fails, check the connection and retry the required format; the preview alone is not confirmation that the full file downloaded.

sections.title: High-Detail Town Maps
paragraphs: High-Detail Town Maps are downloadable town-map files in My Directory. They are separate from printing or exporting one of your own My Maps.

articles.title: Understand which activities appear in Care Calendar
articles.summary: Understand the reviewed schedule sources available for personal activity planning.

sections.title: Use Care Calendar
paragraphs: Open Care Calendar from your dashboard to view supported saved Offering schedules and your personal plans. Saving an Offering does not guarantee it has a supported schedule to show in Care Calendar, and a personal plan is not a provider booking or registration. Review source changes before relying on dates, and confirm attendance with the provider. Unsaving an Offering in My Directory can remove its saved calendar source.

articles.title: Add a session to My Plans and arrange booking with the provider
articles.summary: Record intended attendance and arrange registration directly with the provider.

sections.title: Record a plan, then arrange attendance with the provider
paragraphs: My Plans records intended attendance. Adding a session does not reserve a place, register you or pay the provider.
Sign in to the account that will keep the personal plan. The Programme/service must be saved and have a current active dated session available to plan.
steps: Save the Programme/service, then open Care Calendar → Calendar.
On a current active session, choose Add to My Plans.
If This overlaps another plan appears, review the named conflicts. Select Add anyway only if you intend that overlap, or Cancel to leave the new session unplanned.
Open My Plans and check the Programme/service name, date and time before relying on your plan.
Check the provider’s current eligibility, fees, availability and registration process, and arrange attendance directly with the provider.
notes: The Guide cannot book a seat or contact the provider for you.
To remove your personal plan, use Remove from My Plans. This does not cancel a provider booking.
If a save reports an error, check My Plans before retrying. If no active session is available, check current dates with the provider rather than assuming a saved listing has bookable sessions.

sections.title: Add a saved activity session to My Plans
paragraphs: Save the Offering first, then open Care Calendar and choose Calendar. On an active session, choose Add to My Plans. If it overlaps another plan, review the conflict warning before deciding whether to add it anyway. My Plans records intended attendance only; it is not a provider booking or registration. Confirm attendance with the provider.

sections.title: Plans are not bookings
paragraphs: A personal plan records intended attendance. It is not a booking, registration, or confirmation from the provider. Check the provider’s current details and contact them when registration is needed.

sections.title: Who planned a provider Programme
paragraphs: The Guide cannot show a provider who added its Programme/service to My Plans, how many people planned it, or a member or attendee list. My Plans is private to each signed-in account; the Calendar read and removal paths check that account. A personal plan is not a registration or verified attendance record. Ask the provider about its own registration process if an official attendance list is needed, without putting member details in Guide chat.

articles.title: Review schedule changes, cancellations and Updates
articles.summary: Review changes without assuming an earlier plan has moved or been rebooked.

sections.title: Review a changed or cancelled planned session
paragraphs: Sign in to the account that made the plan. Use Care Calendar’s Updates when a session you added to My Plans has changed; your earlier choice is not moved automatically.
steps: Open Care Calendar and select Updates.
Find the Programme/service with a change. Compare the dates and times under Your affected plans with Current sessions.
If you no longer want an earlier plan, select Remove old plan on that exact entry. This removes your personal calendar plan immediately.
If a suitable current active session is offered, select Add to My Plans on that session. If it already says In My Plans, it is already in your list.
Open My Plans to check the session you chose. Check current details and any registration separately with the provider.
Return to Updates and select Acknowledge update when you have finished reviewing the change. This clears the notice; it does not choose a replacement for you.
notes: If there are no active replacement sessions, do not assume your old date is still available. Open the activity for the latest details or contact the provider.
Removing an old plan, adding a replacement and acknowledging a notice are separate actions. None changes the provider’s schedule or cancels or creates a provider booking.
If a calendar action reports an error, check My Plans and Updates again before deciding whether to retry. Hidden or unpublished sessions can leave earlier personal plans for you to review.

sections.title: Review a changed planned session
paragraphs: If an Offering schedule changes after you add a session to My Plans, your old choice is not moved automatically. Open Care Calendar > Updates to compare affected plans with current sessions. Remove an old plan and choose Add to My Plans on a current active session if needed. Acknowledging the update removes the notice; it does not add a new plan or book you with the provider. Recheck details with the provider before relying on a date.

sections.title: Hiding a Programme and existing personal plans
paragraphs: Hiding a Programme/service does not automatically delete an existing personal plan. While hidden, its current sessions are not offered as Care Calendar occurrences; turning off or unpublishing its sessions likewise does not delete a personal plan. A person can still see their own earlier plan in My Plans and may need to review a changed schedule in Updates. A plan is not a provider booking. The Guide cannot identify who planned the Programme or edit another person’s plans; check current details with the provider before relying on an old date.

articles.title: Manage a dated personal reminder, if supported
articles.summary: Use dated map notes and review the difference between a note date and a provider session.

sections.title: Add a dated private map note to Care Calendar
paragraphs: Sign in and use a My Map you own. This workflow dates a saved note attached to a map resource; it is not a general appointment form or a provider booking.
steps: Open My Directory → My Maps and open your map.
Open Map Notes and select the resource you want the note to describe.
Enter the note and wait for its save to finish. Keep Share this note off if the note should remain private.
Select Add to calendar beneath the saved, non-empty note.
In Add this private note to your calendar, enter Calendar title and Starts. Enter Ends (optional) if you need an end time. Use Singapore time.
Select Add to calendar. Care Calendar opens the day containing the new entry; check its title, date and time there.
notes: Add to calendar appears only after the note has been saved and contains text. If saving fails, resolve the note error and use Save notes before continuing.
Cancel closes the calendar form without adding an entry. The saved map note remains available.
Only you can see the dated calendar item. Sharing the original note is a separate map setting; do not put private or medical details in a shared note.
If adding the calendar entry reports an error, check that day before retrying so you do not intentionally create a second reminder for the same note.

sections.title: Move or remove a dated private map note
paragraphs: Use the calendar entry for your own saved map note. The current calendar cards offer removal; to choose another date through the app, remove that entry and add the saved note again.
steps: Open Care Calendar, select Calendar, and open the day containing the dated note.
Check the note’s title and time, then select Remove private map note on that entry. This removes the calendar item immediately.
To give the note another date, reopen its original resource in your map’s Map Notes and select Add to calendar on the saved note.
Enter the new Calendar title, Starts and any Ends (optional), then select Add to calendar. Check the new entry on its calendar day.
notes: Removing this calendar item does not delete the original map note. Stop after removal if you do not want another reminder.
If you see Remove from My Plans instead, the entry is a provider session. Use a current session offered by that provider rather than inventing a different session time.
If removal fails, check whether the old entry is still present before adding another one. A dated private note does not register you with a provider.

sections.title: Remove a Programme/service session from My Plans
paragraphs: Sign in to the account that added the session. This removes your personal plan only.
steps: Open Care Calendar and select My Plans.
Find the planned Programme/service session and check its name, date and time.
Select Remove from My Plans on that session. The action removes that personal plan immediately.
Check My Plans to confirm the entry has gone. If you registered with the provider, contact them separately about cancelling or changing that booking.
notes: This does not delete or change the provider’s Programme/service listing or schedule.
If you want a different provider session, add a current active session when one is available. If the removal reports an error, check the list before retrying.

sections.title: Add a personal date to Care Calendar
paragraphs: Care Calendar shows planned sessions from saved Programmes/services and dated notes from your own My Maps. To add a personal date linked to a map resource, open that resource’s Map Notes, save a note, choose Add to Calendar, then enter its title and date. I cannot verify a general appointment-entry button outside those supported sources. A calendar entry is personal planning, not a provider booking.

sections.title: Change the date of a personal plan
paragraphs: If your plan is a provider Programme/service session, its time follows that provider’s schedule. Remove the old session from My Plans and add a different current active session if one is offered; changing your plan does not change the provider’s schedule or registration. If you mean a dated My Map note, remove its calendar entry and use Add to Calendar on the saved note to choose another date.

sections.title: Remove a session from My Plans
paragraphs: Open Care Calendar → My Plans and choose Remove from My Plans on the planned session. This removes your own calendar plan; it does not delete the provider’s Programme/service listing or cancel a provider booking. Check with the provider separately if you registered with them.

articles.title: Update profile and location preferences
articles.summary: Update private profile details in Profile and understand eligibility limits.

sections.title: Review and save your profile details
paragraphs: Sign in to your own account. Enter personal details in Profile, not in Guide chat.
steps: Open Dashboard → Profile. On a phone, open the dashboard navigation menu and choose Profile.
Review the current fields and edit only the details you intend to change.
If you choose to provide them, review the optional details under Personalise your recommendations, such as date of birth, CHAS card, gender, property type, caregiver status and volunteer interest.
Leave the password fields blank when you are only changing profile or postal-code details.
Select Save changes and wait for Profile updated successfully! before treating the request as complete.
Reopen Profile to check your saved details. If you arrived from a restricted Programme/service prompt, return to that listing and check it again.
notes: Completing a field does not guarantee access or eligibility, join a Place, register you with a provider, or establish resource-editing rights. Confirm participation requirements with the provider.

An account with an existing registered email cannot change it in this profile form. Adding recovery email/password to a WhatsApp-first account is a separate recovery workflow; do not start it just to change other details.
If saving displays an error, read the message, reopen Profile to check what is currently stored and correct the affected field before retrying. The Guide cannot save profile changes for you.
If you are using User View, exit it before changing profile details. Never paste passwords, identity numbers or medical details into chat.

sections.title: Set or change your home postal code
paragraphs: Your profile postal code helps CareAround show nearby resources and information for your service area. It is not a public Place address or a Personal place pin.
steps: Sign in and open Dashboard → Profile.
Find Postal code (recommended) on a standard user account, or the Postal code field shown for your account.
Enter the correct six-digit Singapore postal code for your home location. Do not put a resource’s postal code here merely to change that resource’s listing.
Review the rest of the form and leave password fields blank if you are only updating the postal code.
Select Save changes and wait for Profile updated successfully!.
Reopen Profile to check the saved value, then return to Discover and review the nearby results.
notes: A standard user can leave the postal code blank or clear it and save if they do not want a home postal code stored. Some operational account roles require a postal code; follow the field validation for your own account.

If the postal code is rejected, check all six digits and the displayed message before trying again. After any save error, reopen Profile to check the stored value rather than assuming all changes were accepted.
A home postal code does not guarantee eligibility for a Programme/service or register you. Profile criteria, membership and provider participation requirements are separate.
Keep your home postal code and other private profile details out of Guide chat. Changing the profile field does not create, move or publish a map location.

sections.title: Update your profile
paragraphs: Sign in, open Profile from the dashboard, update the fields you want to change, and choose Save Changes. Some details help CareAround evaluate restricted Programme/service criteria, but completing your profile does not guarantee eligibility or register you with a provider. Enter private details in Profile, not Guide chat.

sections.title: Missing profile details for restricted offerings
paragraphs: When a Programme/service uses profile criteria and a required field is missing, CareAround can leave the access check unresolved. Complete the relevant field in your Profile and check the listing again. A missing field does not prove you qualify, explain every visibility difference, or register you with the provider; keep personal details out of Guide chat.

sections.title: Ask about deleting an account
paragraphs: The Guide cannot delete your account or confirm that your personal data has been erased. I cannot verify a self-service deletion path here. Use Help to ask support for the current account-deletion process; describe your request without passwords, identity numbers or medical details. Sending a request is not confirmation that deletion has happened.

articles.title: Choose language, contrast and text size
articles.summary: Use app language, contrast and text-size controls for readability.

sections.title: Switch the app language
paragraphs: You can change the app language from the top navigation without signing in.
steps: Find the Language selector in the top navigation.
Select English, Mandarin, Malay or Tamil. On a narrow screen, the same choices appear as EN, 中文, MS and TA.
Check the page after the language changes. Select another language from the same control whenever you need to switch back.
notes: The choice applies immediately and is remembered in this browser; there is no separate Save button for it.
Provider-written information may use its original language. Guide and support are currently in English, so changing the app language does not translate every answer.

sections.title: Change contrast and text size on desktop or a phone
paragraphs: These controls change how the app is displayed. They do not change resource details or provider-written information.
steps: On a wide screen, find Contrast and the A- / A+ controls in the top navigation. On a phone or narrow screen, select the sun or moon button labelled Open accessibility controls to open Accessibility.
On a wide screen, select Contrast to enable high contrast; select Normal to return to the normal display. In Accessibility, use Turn on high contrast or Return to normal contrast.
Select A+ to increase text size or A- to reduce it. A+ becomes unavailable at the maximum size supported for the current screen.
Check the text and controls on your page. Adjust again if needed.
On a narrow screen, select Done to close Accessibility. Your display changes apply without a separate Save action.
notes: Contrast and text size are remembered in this browser. Clearing browser storage can reset them.
Text size has limits, and the maximum can change with the screen width. These controls do not guarantee that every image, map label or provider-written detail will become larger or clearer.

sections.title: Adjust contrast and text size
paragraphs: Use the top navigation’s contrast control and A− / A+ controls to adjust readability. On a narrow screen, open the accessibility control to find these options. The controls apply to the app display and do not change a provider’s original information.

sections.title: Change the app language
paragraphs: Use the Language selector in the top navigation. The app offers English, Mandarin, Malay and Tamil; on a narrow screen the choices may appear as short labels such as 中文. This changes the app language. Check a particular provider listing directly if its own wording is missing or unclear.

articles.title: Verify or link a phone using the available account controls
articles.summary: Review saved-phone and verification states using the available Profile controls.

sections.title: Verify your saved phone with WhatsApp
paragraphs: Sign in and open your own Profile. A phone number typed into the form is not yet a verified WhatsApp identity; save the correct number before starting verification.
steps: Open dashboard → Profile and check the Phone number field.
If the number needs changing, enter it and select Save changes. Recheck the saved number before continuing.
In the phone verification panel, select Verify with WhatsApp. If you changed an already linked number, use Verify new WhatsApp number when that is the action shown.
Follow the WhatsApp instructions for that verification attempt. If WhatsApp did not open, use Open WhatsApp when it is available.
Return to Profile and keep the page open while verification is checked. If the panel is still waiting, select Check again when offered.
Read the result in the panel. Completion is shown as WhatsApp phone verified; an unsuccessful or pending result is not verification.
notes: Do not start several attempts at once or paste verification messages or codes into Guide chat or a support report.

For a failed or expired attempt, use Try again when the panel offers it. If it says Needs help, follow the displayed reason and contact CareAround support rather than repeatedly starting verification; Refresh status is available for those review states.
