Changing the Profile phone does not immediately replace a previously verified phone. The panel can show the current verified phone and a new saved phone separately until the new verification succeeds.
If a Profile save reports an error, reopen Profile and check the saved number before verifying. The Guide cannot complete verification for you.

sections.title: Remove an existing verified WhatsApp link
paragraphs: Use this only if the phone verification panel shows Remove verified WhatsApp link. Read the consequence before confirming.
steps: Open your own Profile and check the current verified phone in the verification panel.
Select Remove verified WhatsApp link.
Read the confirmation: removing WhatsApp verification does not delete your account or its contact number. Cancel if you do not want to unlink.
To proceed, select Remove verified WhatsApp link in the confirmation, then check the panel’s updated status.
notes: If the app says to add a recovery email and password before unlinking, complete the required recovery setup first. The Guide cannot bypass this requirement or unlink the phone in chat.
If unlinking reports an error, check the current status before retrying. Saving a contact number, verifying it and removing its WhatsApp link are separate account actions.

sections.title: Use the phone controls shown in Profile
paragraphs: Save the phone number in Profile before starting its available verification action. Follow the WhatsApp prompt and return to the app to review its verification status. The panel offers different controls for pending, failed, expired or changed numbers; use the action shown for your current status.
notes: Avoid starting several attempts at once. Do not paste verification messages or codes into Guide chat or a support report.
A phone saved in Profile and a verified sign-in identity are related but separate states. Read the current panel status before assuming verification is complete.
If the app requires manual review or a recovery method, follow that message or report the access problem. The Guide cannot verify or unlink the phone for you.

articles.title: Link a Place membership using its approved QR code or link
articles.summary: Review linked Place memberships and distinguish them from bookmarks and registration.

sections.title: Join the intended Place through its membership QR code or link
paragraphs: Use the membership QR code or link provided for the Place you intend to join. Check that intention before opening it: for a signed-in account, opening a valid membership link starts linking automatically, without another Join confirmation button.
steps: Sign in to the CareAround account that should receive the Place membership.
Check with the Place that you have its intended membership QR code or link. A normal public listing link or the save heart is a different action.
Scan the membership QR code or open the membership link. If CareAround asks you to sign in, use the intended account and return through that flow.
Wait for the linking result. On success, check You’re now linked and the Place name shown in Your account has been linked to [Place name].
Open dashboard → Profile and scroll below the profile form to Linked places. Check the Place, its status and linking method there.
notes: Authorised Place managers can see membership details, including names. This is not the same as a private bookmark.
Membership can help with member-only eligibility, but does not register you for a Programme/service, grant resource editing rights, or automatically save the Place or its programmes in My Directory.
If the link is missing, invalid or fails, ask the Place for the correct current membership link. Do not assume you joined unless the success result or your Linked places confirms it.
The Guide cannot grant membership, remove another person’s membership or confirm your personal membership records from a general question.

sections.title: Linked Place membership
paragraphs: A Place membership link can connect your signed-in account to that Place and may help with access to member-only Programmes/services. Other eligibility rules can still apply. Linking membership does not register you for a Programme/service or give you permission to edit the Place; check registration with the provider.

sections.title: Review your linked Place memberships
paragraphs: To check your linked Place memberships yourself, sign in and open dashboard → Profile. Scroll below the profile form to Linked places, which shows Places joined through the membership QR flow, their status and the linking method. You do not need to send your personal profile fields to the Guide. This reply has not checked your membership records or confirmed that you belong to any Place. Linked places is separate from saved resources in My Directory and from resources you can edit in Manage My Resources; membership does not grant editing rights or Programme registration.

sections.title: Private bookmarks and Place membership
paragraphs: Saving with the heart is a private bookmark in your My Directory. Joining a Place through its membership link or QR connects your signed-in account to that Place; it is a separate membership, not a saved resource. Authorised Place managers can see membership details, including names. Saving does not create that membership, and joining does not automatically save the Place or its Programme/service. Membership may help with member-only eligibility, but it does not register you for a Programme/service or grant editing rights. Review your memberships in Profile and your bookmarks in My Directory.

sections.title: Programme host Places and personal membership
paragraphs: A Programme/service’s Host Locations connect that listing to one or more public Places. A personal Place membership connects a signed-in person’s account to a Place through its membership link; these are separate relationships. Linking or changing a Programme’s host Places does not make you a member of those Places, register you for the Programme, or give you editing rights. People who saved the listing are not enrolled by that host change. A member-only Programme may require an active membership at a linked Place and other eligibility checks. An authorised manager changes hosts in the Offering editor; you can review your own Place membership in Profile. The Guide cannot grant membership, confirm your eligibility or edit an existing listing in chat.

sections.title: Another person’s Place memberships
paragraphs: The Guide cannot check or list another person’s Place memberships in this chat. Linked places in Profile shows the signed-in account’s own memberships; it is not a lookup of someone else. This reply has not checked anyone’s membership records or confirmed which Places they have joined. Place membership is separate from saving a resource, editing it and registering for a Programme/service. Keep personal profile details out of chat.

articles.title: Ask the Guide, read its sources and use help when AI is unavailable
articles.summary: Ask about CareAround tasks, follow reviewed sources and find manual help when AI is unavailable.

sections.title: Ask a product question and use its sources
paragraphs: Yes. You can still read the public Help Centre without AI. Open the CareAround Help Centre to search for your task and read its complete reviewed instructions. Use the app’s normal controls to carry out the task; an unanswered Guide request has not created, saved or changed anything. Sign in for account-specific guidance and checks.
steps: Open Help → Guide & search and select Open CareAround Guide. Enter your CareAround question in the Guide and send it.
Read the response. Under Related reviewed guidance, select the article title to open its complete instructions when a source is offered.
If the question concerns this account, sign in and use the supported current-account checks. A general help answer has not inspected your records.

If AI is unavailable, open the CareAround Help Centre, use Search for your task, and read the reviewed article. Use the app’s manual controls to carry out the task; an unanswered request has not changed anything.
notes: The Guide supports CareAround product help. Confirm provider eligibility, fees and availability with the provider.
Use Report a problem for a reproducible app issue; keep passwords, verification codes and sensitive personal information out of chat.

sections.title: Read the Help Centre without AI
paragraphs: Yes. You can still read the public Help Centre without AI. You do not need to send a Guide question or wait for an AI response before reading the instructions.
steps: Open the CareAround Help Centre.
Choose a category under Browse by topic, or enter your task or a button name in Search help articles and select Search.
Open the matching article and read its numbered steps and notes. If there is no match, try a shorter search or select Show all help articles.
Return to the relevant app page and follow the instructions using its normal controls. Review and confirm any change before saving it.
notes: An unanswered Guide request has not created, saved or changed anything. Reading instructions does not perform the task for you.
Public Help Centre articles can be read without signing in. Sign in when the task needs account-specific checks; reading help does not grant account access or permission to make changes.

sections.title: Keep private information out of chat
paragraphs: Do not include identity numbers, passwords, verification codes, medical histories, private notes, or private sharing links. Support only needs a description of the app problem. The Guide cannot give medical advice or confirm provider eligibility, fees, or availability.

sections.title: Provider usage information in the Guide
paragraphs: The Guide cannot look up a provider report showing how many people viewed or saved a particular Place or Offering, or identify those people. Manage My Resources shows listing-management controls, which are different from usage analytics. I cannot verify a provider-facing usage report from Guide chat. If your organisation needs an official report, describe that need in a support report without putting other people’s details in chat.

articles.title: Check your own current account access through the Guide
articles.summary: Distinguish a general permission explanation from a supported authenticated account check.

sections.title: Ask about this account’s access
paragraphs: Ask a specific question such as whether this account can manage resources. Supported account checks use the signed-in account’s permissions. They do not grant access or inspect another person’s account.
notes: If you are in User View, exit User View before checking your own resource permissions or using Guide actions.
Current-account replies and general product explanations have different proof: an article explains a rule; a supported authenticated check reports this account’s current result.

sections.title: Another person’s saved resources
paragraphs: The Guide reads only the signed-in account’s saved resources and cannot show a colleague’s saved list from your chat. A colleague may choose to share a selected My Map snapshot, but that is separate from their whole My Directory. Do not use another person’s sign-in details; open My Directory for your own saved resources.

sections.title: Checking what a provider has received
paragraphs: The Guide cannot check whether a provider has received your name or personal information. It cannot inspect the provider’s messages, registration records or contact history. Saving a listing does not send your profile to its provider, but that does not establish what the provider received through membership, registration or other contact. For confirmation, contact the provider using the channels on its listing if available. This chat has not contacted the provider or verified delivery.

sections.title: Other people’s account permissions
paragraphs: The Guide cannot check another person’s Group Admin role from chat. The Guide cannot check another person’s Organisation Admin role or show their memberships from chat. Ask about this signed-in account’s own current access instead. An article explains the rules; it does not prove anyone’s role.

articles.title: Review and confirm a supported Guide action
articles.summary: Review the supported action before choosing Create or Save.

sections.title: Review and create a new Programme/service with the Guide
paragraphs: Sign in, exit User View if it is active, and use a Place your account is permitted to manage. Guide actions must be enabled; this workflow creates a new Programme/service rather than editing an existing listing.
steps: Open Ask Guide and select Create a programme/service, or ask it to create a Programme/service.
In the Programme/service draft, enter Name and Type. Search Linked place and choose the exact Place you can manage.
Choose Visibility and review its explanation. Complete Description and Contact details if needed. Hidden from directory is not a promise that nobody with permitted access can see it.

For real calendar sessions, open Dates & recurrence, enable Add dated sessions for Care Calendar, and enter the actual dates and times in Singapore time. Requested timing text alone does not create dated sessions.
Select Review programme/service. In Create this programme/service?, check the type, name, linked Place, visibility, description, contact details and any calendar dates.
Use Edit draft if anything needs changing, then review again. Only when the details are correct, select Create programme/service to confirm saving the real resource.
Wait for the message that the Programme/service has been created and open its returned resource link to check the result.
notes: A prepared draft or review is not a saved resource. Creating uses your account’s existing permissions, which are checked by the server; it does not book anyone into a service.
Before creation, Discard draft clears the chat draft. It does not delete an already saved Programme/service.
If the save result is not confirmed, keep the conversation open and use Retry same request to check or complete that reviewed request safely. Do not start another draft to recreate it.
If the panel says the saved request has changed or cannot be reconciled, open Manage resources and check your resources before starting another draft.

No matching manageable Place means you must check your resource access rather than assume the Guide can grant it. New public Places, Resource Groups and changes to existing listings use their permitted standard forms.

sections.title: Review a Guide search result before saving it
paragraphs: Sign in to use the Guide’s resource save action. Searching uses public directory keywords rather than your private profile.
steps: Open Ask Guide and select Find and save a resource, or expand Search the public directory.
Enter Resource keywords, choose the resource type, and select Search directory.
Find the intended public result and select Review save. If it already says Saved in My Directory, it is already saved.
Check the name, type and address in Save [resource name] to My Directory?. Use Cancel if it is the wrong result.
Select Save to My Directory to confirm the save.
Wait for Saved or Already saved, then select Open My Directory to check your private list.
notes: Saving does not register you with the provider, grant management rights, or add the resource to a My Map. Check dates, fees, availability and registration with the provider.
If no public match appears, try a shorter name, service or address, or use Continue in Discover. If saving reports an error, check My Directory before retrying the same resource save.
Save this search is a separate action that keeps search criteria; it does not save every result.

sections.title: What the Guide can create
paragraphs: The Guide’s direct Create action currently supports a Programme/service at a Place your account may manage: prepare a draft, review it, then choose Create. The Guide cannot submit a new public Place or Resource Group from chat. Those use the existing New Place or New Group forms in Manage My Resources when your account has permission.

sections.title: What the Guide can edit
paragraphs: The Guide cannot edit an existing public Place or Offering, including its schedule. It can prepare a new Programme/service for your review and explicit Create when your account may manage its Place. To change an existing listing, open Manage My Resources, choose that exact resource and select Edit if available. Review and save the change there; the server checks permission for that listing.

articles.title: Report a problem, use Inbox and recover a guest report
articles.summary: Report an app issue, follow replies and check current in-app notification limits.

sections.title: Write, review and send an app problem report
paragraphs: You can submit an app problem report while signed in or as a guest. Exit User View before using the support inbox or report form. Keep the report about the app issue.
steps: Open Help and select Report a problem.
Enter a Short title and describe What happened?. Add What did you expect? (optional) if it helps explain the issue.
Choose whether to Include the page where I opened Help (page name only). It is off unless you select it.
Select Review before sending. Read the exact text that will be saved and check for private information. Select Edit report if it needs changing.

If reporting as a guest, select Show code to copy and keep the private recovery code somewhere safe. Select I have saved my recovery code somewhere private before sending. Also remember it in this browser tab is optional.
Select Send report to submit the reviewed report.
Check the conversation opened in Inbox. Use that conversation to follow replies and progress.
notes: The support team can read submitted reports. No screenshot is captured automatically, and unrelated Guide questions are not copied into a report draft you chose from chat.

Keep passwords, verification codes, identity numbers, medical details and private links out of the report. Automatic removal of recognisable links and credential-like text does not replace your own review.
A guest code gives anyone who has it access to read and reply for 30 days after the report is created. CareAround cannot recover a lost code for you; do not put it in another report.
If sending reports an error, your draft remains available. Check the Inbox for the report before retrying. A reviewed draft has not yet been submitted.

sections.title: Read replies and resolve or reopen your report
paragraphs: Use the account that submitted the report, or recover the guest report with its private code. Account reports are available only to you and authorised support reviewers.
steps: Open Help → Inbox. For an account inbox, select Messages.
Select the report by its title. Use Refresh inbox if you need to refresh the list; Load older reports appears when another page is available.
Read its messages and status. Use Load newer messages when offered, and select Mark shown messages read after reading the messages displayed.
If a reply is needed, enter Your reply and select Send reply. Keep it about the app issue and leave private details out.
When the problem is fixed for you, select Mark resolved. If a fix-available update has not solved it, select Problem remains — reopen instead.
If an already resolved problem returns, open its report and select Reopen report. Check the updated status before continuing the conversation.
notes: An unresolved report offers the reply form; reopen a resolved report before adding a new reply. Marking shown messages read does not claim that unseen messages were read.
Use Refresh conversation to check current replies and status. If an action reports an error, refresh before retrying.
A proposed fix still needs human approval and release verification before a fix-available update. A support status is not a promise that your reported behaviour has already been fixed.

sections.title: Open a guest report using its private recovery code
paragraphs: Use the complete private recovery code you saved before submitting the guest report. You do not need to sign in to recover it, and the code is not an account sign-in credential.
steps: Open Help and select Inbox. If you are signed in, stay on Messages.
Open Recover a guest report. It is already expanded when you are not signed in and no guest report is open.
Enter your complete code in Private recovery code and select Open guest report.
Check the guest-report banner and select the recovered report to read or reply. Opening a guest report while signed in does not attach it to your account.
When finished, select Close and forget this code if you are a guest, or Return to account inbox if you are signed in. This clears the remembered code from this browser tab.
notes: Codes expire 30 days after the report is created, even if you reopen it later. Anyone with the code can read and reply, so keep it private.
If the code is incomplete, use the full saved code. If it is lost or expired, the app cannot recover it for you; submit a new report without exposing the old code.
Close and forget this code or Return to account inbox closes guest access in this tab; it does not delete the report or attach it to an account.

sections.title: Choose saved-resource updates in your private Inbox
paragraphs: Sign in to use account Updates. Saved-resource notifications, calendar review decisions and support Messages are separate parts of the app.
steps: Open Help → Inbox and select Updates.
Open Notification preferences and enable Saved schedule changes or Saved resource changes as needed. Each choice is saved when you change its checkbox.
If the panel says in-app notifications are disabled in Profile, select Open Profile. Under Pilot preferences, enable In-app and select Save notification preferences.
Return to Inbox → Updates → Notification preferences. If a resource you want to hear about is under Muted resources, select Unmute for that resource.
Use Refresh updates to check your current Inbox. Open the relevant resource or calendar action on an update before deciding what to change.
notes: Checks run after changes rather than promising an instant alert. Enabling a category or unmuting starts from current information and does not produce catch-up alerts.
These choices do not move My Plans entries or register you with a provider. The Guide can explain them but cannot change them from chat.
Email, WhatsApp and SMS choices in Profile record preferences only in the current pilot; external delivery remains disabled. Inbox updates do not send device push messages.
If preference saving reports an error, reload the controls and check the stored choices before retrying.

sections.title: Report a problem and follow its progress
paragraphs: Describe what happened and what you expected, review the report, then submit it. Replies and progress updates stay in your inbox. A proposed fix needs human approval and release verification before a fix-available update is sent. You can confirm it is resolved or reopen it if the problem remains.

sections.title: Changing notification preferences outside Guide chat
paragraphs: The Guide can explain notification controls, but cannot change your preferences, mute or unmute resources, or enable message delivery from chat. To choose saved-resource updates, open Inbox → Updates → Notification preferences. For schedule changes, enable Saved schedule changes there, enable in-app notifications in Profile, and make sure that resource is not muted. Email, WhatsApp and SMS preferences do not enable external delivery in the current pilot. The Guide has not changed any setting and cannot confirm your current preferences or that an alert has fired from this general question.

sections.title: In-app and external notification channels
paragraphs: In-app Updates and external messages are different. In the current CareAround notification pilot, email, WhatsApp and SMS choices in Profile record preferences only; external delivery remains disabled even when those choices are enabled. For a saved Programme schedule update, open Inbox → Updates and enable Saved schedule changes in Notification preferences. Profile in-app notifications must be enabled and that resource must not be muted. The Guide cannot confirm that a particular alert has fired from this general question. WhatsApp sign-in and contacting a provider are separate workflows.

sections.title: Updates when a saved Programme schedule changes
paragraphs: A saved Programme/service can produce an in-app Saved schedule changes update after its published Care Calendar schedule changes. Open Inbox → Updates and enable Saved schedule changes in Notification preferences. In-app notifications must also be enabled in Profile, and that resource must not be muted. Checks run after a change rather than promising an instant alert; enabling or unmuting starts from current information without a catch-up alert. This does not move your My Plans entry or book with the provider. The Guide cannot verify that a particular alert has fired from a general question.

articles.title: Understand assigned resource permissions and missing controls
articles.summary: Check the exact resource’s permission rather than inferring access from a title or saved entry.

sections.title: Add or remove authorised Staff or Owner access for a saved Place
paragraphs: Use this workflow only as a Super Admin or an active Owner of this exact Place. Being able to edit it as Staff is not permission to assign other people. The Place must already be saved.
steps: Sign in and open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Places. Find the exact Place and select Edit if available.
Open Access and review Current access, including the existing Owners and Staff. Use Refresh if you need to reload the current assignments.
In Add access, search under User, choose the intended eligible account from Select user, and choose Staff or Owner from the roles available to you. Check the person and role before continuing.
Select Add access and wait for the result. This saves the assignment immediately; check the refreshed Current access list rather than expecting Save Place to submit it later.
To revoke an existing assignment when permitted, choose Remove on that exact person’s row, review Remove access?, and select Remove only if that is intended. Their platform account is not deleted.

Verify the refreshed list. If adding or removing fails, read the error and ask the appropriate Owner or administrator to review the target’s eligibility and current assignment; do not try to bypass a missing control.
notes: The server checks the assigning account, the target’s organisation eligibility and any existing active assignment. An unavailable search result does not prove the person lacks a CareAround account.
The final active Owner cannot be removed through this workflow. Do not remove a responsible Owner before arranging an approved replacement.
Add access and confirmed Remove are saved independently of profile edits. Closing the Place editor or choosing Cancel does not undo an access change that has succeeded.
Adding an individual Owner is not a transfer of a Place to another organisation. Use the support route for review of a true organisation-ownership transfer.
Keep names, account contact details and assignment screenshots within authorised operational channels. The Guide cannot add, remove or transfer access in chat.

sections.title: Owner and Staff access is scoped to each Place
paragraphs: An active Owner or Staff assignment applies to the exact Place assigned. Being an Owner of one Place does not grant editing or management rights over every Place. Super Admin access is a separate exception; an organisation or Region Admin role alone is not a Place edit assignment. Open Manage My Resources and check Edit on the exact Place; the server checks current permission again before saving. This explains the rule, not whether your account currently has an assignment to a particular Place. The Guide cannot grant access or edit an existing listing for you.

sections.title: Region Admin and Place editing
paragraphs: A Region Admin role alone does not grant Edit on every Place. Current Place edit permission depends on Super Admin access or an active Owner or Staff assignment to that exact Place. Regional management visibility is separate from the listing’s Edit control; choose the exact Place in Manage My Resources to check its current permission. The server checks again before saving.

sections.title: Can a volunteer create a Place
paragraphs: “Volunteer” is a person’s title; it does not establish their CareAround account’s permission to use New Place. Place creation depends on the signed-in account’s resource role or partner resource-staff access, and the selected location and scope are checked when saving. The person should use their own account to check New Place in Manage My Resources. The Guide cannot submit a public Place from chat.

sections.title: Edit a Place or Offering
paragraphs: Open Manage My Resources, choose Places or Offerings, then open the resource card and choose Edit if that control is available. Save the changes in its editor. Editing depends on the selected resource and is checked again by the server; appearing in My Directory because you saved it is not editing access. A template-generated Place version has inherited fields, so edit its parent template for those shared details.

sections.title: Assign staff to a Place
paragraphs: Open Manage My Resources, edit the saved Place, then open its Access step. Only a Super Admin or an Owner of that particular Place can add Staff or Owners; being able to edit as Staff is not enough. The server checks the target account’s organisation eligibility and existing access before saving. The Guide cannot add or remove staff.

sections.title: Place ownership transfer versus staff access
paragraphs: I cannot verify a self-service control to transfer a Place to another organisation in the current Place editor, and the Guide cannot perform that transfer. The Place’s Access step manages individual Owners and Staff when the current account is allowed to do so; adding an Owner is not an organisation-ownership transfer. If a true transfer is needed, use Help to request review of the exact Place and intended organisation without sharing passwords or private account details.

sections.title: Organisation membership and listing editing are separate
paragraphs: No. Organisation membership or a governance role alone does not grant permission to edit its Place or Programme/service listings. Organisation workspace access and resource-editing assignments are separate.

Editing depends on an active Owner or Staff assignment to the exact resource, or Super Admin access. Open Manage My Resources and check Edit on the selected listing; the server checks current permission again before saving. This is the general rule, not confirmation of your account’s assignments. The Guide cannot grant access.

articles.title: Create or maintain a public Place
articles.summary: Use the authorised public listing workflow instead of a private Personal place.

sections.title: Create a public Place with the New Place form
paragraphs: Use New Place for an approved public directory listing, not a private meeting point or a location only for your own map. Sign in with the resource permission needed for New Place; job title, saved resources and organisation membership do not by themselves establish that permission.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources and select New Place if that control is available.

In Profile, enter Name and choose Category. Add a clear public description, website and approved public media where needed. Leave the optional External Key blank unless you are following an approved workbook process.
Open Location. For a Singapore Place, choose Country → Singapore, enter its verified six-digit Postal code and Street Address, and review the service-area message.
Add the public Phone, WhatsApp contact, Contact email and Hours when available. Verify these with the provider; the WhatsApp contact is a public contact field, not a sign-in number.
Open Visibility. Review Hide from App and any Scheduled Hide (From) or Scheduled Hide (Until) values so the Place has the intended availability.
Select Preview and check the profile, address, contacts and visibility. Close the preview, correct any errors, then select Save Place.
Wait for a successful save and reopen the Place to verify it. Access, Zones, Translate and Restricted tools require the resource to exist before you manage them.
notes: If New Place is missing, ask an authorised resource manager to check your account’s current permission; the Guide cannot create a public Place in chat.

If postal validation fails, check the real six-digit Singapore code and address. A service-area warning is not permission to guess a location. Where the editor offers Singapore fallback validation, saving still checks the code on the server.
A Place that is saved but hidden is not automatically visible in Discover. Public details should contain approved provider information, not attendee information or private operating notes.
For a point only on your own map, use Personal place instead. It stays private and does not become a public Place.
A failed save is not confirmation of creation. Correct the highlighted required detail or report the issue without sharing credentials.

sections.title: Update a Place’s public profile, location and contacts
paragraphs: You must have Edit permission for the exact Place. Confirm the provider information before changing a public listing.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Places, find the exact Place, and select Edit if available.
In Profile, review its name, category, description, website and public media. Keep the saved External Key unchanged.
Open Location to update Street Address, Postal code, Phone, WhatsApp contact, Contact email or Hours. Recheck the location and service-area message after an address or postal-code change.
Review Visibility and the public Preview so the changes describe the intended Place without exposing private notes.
Select Save Place, wait for success, and reopen the Place to confirm the saved public details.
notes: Saving the Place to My Directory or managing a different listing does not grant Edit here. If Edit is missing, request review of the exact Place assignment.
This changes the Place’s fields, not the Offering-level contact details of every Programme/service linked to it. Maintain those listings in their own editors.
An individual Owner assignment in Access is not a transfer to a different organisation. Access actions also save separately from Save Place.
If a save fails, review the validation message and confirmed provider information. The Guide cannot edit an existing public Place for you.

sections.title: Add or create a resource
paragraphs: Do you mean save an existing resource, create a Programme/service, or add a new Place? To save an existing resource, find it in Discover and use its heart to add it to My Directory. If you manage a Place and want a new Programme/service, ask me to “create a programme” or “create a service”; review the draft and choose Create to save it. To add a new Place, authorized resource managers can open Manage My Resources and choose New Place; that uses the standard resource form.

sections.title: Edit a Place’s public contact details
paragraphs: Open Manage My Resources → Places, open the exact Place and choose Edit if that control is available. In Location, update its public Phone, WhatsApp contact, Contact email or Hours, then review and save. The WhatsApp contact is not a sign-in number. Saving or managing a different resource does not grant editing rights to this Place; the Guide cannot change the listing for you.

articles.title: Create or maintain a Programme/service
articles.summary: Create a Programme/service, review its hosts and visibility, or maintain the correct shared or local details.

sections.title: Create a Programme/service with the standard New Offering form
paragraphs: Use this flow for a new Programme/service listing that is not a template-generated place version. Sign in with an account that has the required resource permissions. Saving a Place to My Directory, joining it as a member, or having organisation access does not by itself grant editing or creation rights.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources and select New Offering if that control is available to your account. Alternatively, in Places, select Add Offering on a Place you may edit; that Place is preselected as the host.
In Profile, enter Name, choose Bucket and Category, and add a clear description. Enter only the public website, contact and action details that people should see for this Programme/service.

Open Schedule. If you have verified dates, turn on Publish sessions and enter the individual sessions or recurring weekly series. Review Public schedule preview and Next generated sessions. If the dates are not ready, leave sessions unpublished; use the related schedule article for the full procedure.

Open Host & coverage. In Host Locations (Optional), select each Place that will host this listing and that your account may manage. Several linked Places must be in the same service area. For a listing without a host, leave Host Locations empty and select at least one Service region, or use a permitted Target area in Visibility.

Open Visibility and review Who can see this? Choose Public or Target areas. For Target areas, select the permitted Audience Zones. Review For linked members and any eligibility rules. In Schedule, check Hide from App and any scheduled hide dates so the listing has the intended visibility.
Select Preview and check the name, description, contacts, host Places, sessions and visibility. Close the preview, correct anything that is wrong, and select Save Offering.

Wait for the successful save, then check the new listing in Offerings. If the form reports an error, correct it and save again; an error or an open draft is not confirmation that the resource was created.
notes: A single Offering linked to several Places has one shared profile, public contact set and structured session schedule. Do not use it for different host-specific contacts or schedules; consider separate listings or the reviewed template/place-version workflow instead.

If New Offering, Add Offering, Edit or a required host is unavailable, stop and ask the appropriate resource owner or administrator to check your exact assignment. These instructions do not establish your account’s current permission, and the server checks each linked Place and final coverage when saving.

If the form says linked Places must be in the same service area, review the chosen hosts rather than forcing an unrelated area. A hostless listing needs at least one allowed Service region or an allowed Target area.

A Resource Group is a separate collection workflow in Groups; it is not a Programme/service created by this form. An Offering template is shared content, not itself a public listing, and generates separately reviewed place versions.

The Guide offers an alternative for one new Programme/service at one manageable Place: prepare a draft, choose Review programme/service, then explicitly choose Create programme/service. The Guide does not create hostless or multi-host listings, Groups or templates, and cannot edit an existing listing in chat.

Public contact and action details belong to this Offering. They do not change the physical Place’s contact fields. Avoid personal attendee details or private contact information; an external registration link does not turn a CareAround listing into a booking.

Saving does not guarantee that every visitor can see the listing. Hidden status, audience areas, linked-member rules and eligibility still apply. Review the related visibility article before publishing.

sections.title: Update an existing Programme/service’s public details and hosts
paragraphs: Before editing, confirm the exact Programme/service and host Places you intend to change. These steps apply to an existing listing with the standard Edit control, not an Edit place version form.
steps: Sign in, open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Offerings, find the exact listing, and select Edit if available.

In Profile, review the name, description and Public contact and action details. Update Contact phone, WhatsApp contact, Contact email, Action button label, Action button link or Venue note as needed, using information approved for public display.

If you are changing hosts, open Host & coverage. Remove the old host from Host Locations and choose the intended replacement, or review all selected hosts for a multi-host listing. Your account must be able to manage each linked Place.
Review Schedule and Visibility after a host or contact change. Check that the sessions, venue instructions, audience, linked-member rule and hide settings still describe the intended listing.
Select Preview to check the changes, close the preview, and select Save Offering. Wait for the successful save, then reopen the listing to verify the saved details.
notes: Editing the Offering’s contacts does not edit its linked Place’s phone, email or other profile fields. A multi-host standalone Offering uses the same Offering-level contacts and sessions across its linked Places.

If Edit is missing or a selected host is unavailable, do not infer access from having saved the resource or from organisation membership. Ask the appropriate owner or administrator to check the exact assignment; the Guide cannot grant permission or move an existing listing in chat.
Changing a host must still satisfy the same-service-area rule for linked Places. When a listing has no linked Place, review its Service regions or permitted Target areas instead.
Use the related schedules article before changing dated sessions. If another person changes the schedule while you save, refresh the Offering and review the latest sessions before trying again.
If the card says Edit place version, use the separate local-version steps below. Those controls do not establish a way to move the generated version to another host.

sections.title: Change only the local details of a template-generated place version
paragraphs: Use this flow when the Programme/service card says Edit place version. A generated version inherits shared content from its Offering template and has separate local details for its fixed host Place.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Offerings and select Edit place version on the exact version you may edit.
Check Inherited from template and Host place so you are editing the intended version. The shared name, category, description, audience and eligibility fields shown there are read-only in this form.
In Local place details, change only the required Local Schedule, Contact Phone, WhatsApp contact, Contact Email, Action button label, Action button link or Venue Note for this host.
Review the version’s local Availability and Hide from app settings and scheduled hide dates. Editing local details does not automatically unhide a hidden version.

Select Save place version, wait for the successful update, then check that version’s public details. Use the related template article if you need to change shared content for several generated versions.
notes: A local schedule or contact override can differ from the parent template. Template edits propagate shared values only where the version has no corresponding local override; review the affected versions before a broad template change.

Reset appears beside an overridden field. Selecting Reset removes that override and reloads the template value immediately; it is a saved change, so do not use Reset merely to preview a value or assume Cancel will undo it.

Local Schedule is a host-specific text field in this editor. It does not offer the standalone form’s Publish sessions switch or structured session rows, so do not promise that typing here creates Care Calendar sessions.

This form’s Host place is read-only. These steps do not establish a rehost control for a generated version. If the wrong host was chosen, ask an authorised template manager to review the supported template workflow.

Use approved public contact details. If the update fails, retain the reported error, refresh the exact version where appropriate, and use the related support article; the Guide cannot save an existing-version edit for you.

sections.title: Change an existing Offering’s linked Place
paragraphs: For an existing standalone Programme/service you can edit, open Manage My Resources → Offerings → Edit → Host & coverage. In Host Locations, remove the old Place and select the new Place, then review the service area, audience, visibility and schedule before saving. If Edit or the new Place is unavailable, this Guide cannot grant access: the server checks your permission for both the Offering and each new linked Place. These steps do not establish a rehost control for a template-generated place version. The Guide cannot move an existing Offering in chat.

sections.title: One Offering linked to several Places
paragraphs: The standard standalone Offering editor can link one Programme/service to multiple Host Locations when those Places are in the same service area. An authorised manager can use New Offering, choose the Places in Host & coverage, then review Visibility and save. The server checks permission for each linked Place and, when editing, the Offering itself. If New Offering or a Place is unavailable, this Guide cannot grant that access. The Guide’s reviewed Create action currently prepares one Place-linked Programme/service; it cannot create one listing across several Places in chat. Template-generated place versions use a separate workflow.

sections.title: Edit an Offering’s public contact details
paragraphs: Open Manage My Resources → Offerings, open the exact Programme/service and choose Edit if available. In Profile → Public contact and action details, update its contact phone, WhatsApp contact, email or action link, then review and save. This changes the Offering’s details, not its linked Place’s contact fields. The server checks your permission for that listing; the Guide cannot edit an existing listing for you.

articles.title: Maintain Programme schedules and sessions
articles.summary: Add individual or weekly sessions, review the public dates, and safely change or unpublish an existing schedule.

sections.title: Add or update individual and recurring Programme sessions
paragraphs: Use these steps for a Programme/service that opens the standard Offering editor. You must be able to edit the exact listing. Confirm dates and times with the provider before publishing; all session times here use Asia/Singapore.
steps: Sign in and open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Offerings. Select Edit on the exact Programme/service. For a new listing, complete Profile in New Offering first.
Open Schedule and turn on Publish sessions. If there are no rows, the editor creates the first session row. If sessions are already published, review the existing rows before changing them.

For a single date, choose Session type → Individual session. Enter Session starts and, if known, Session ends (optional). Choose Status → Scheduled or Cancelled to reflect the provider’s confirmed status, and add a Session note if needed.

For a weekly series, choose Session type → Recurring weekly. Enter the actual first date and time in Series starts, choose the weekdays under Repeats on, and set Session ends and Last repeat date if known. The first date must fall on one of the selected weekdays.

Select Add another schedule for a different session or series. Duplicate copies a row for you to adjust; Remove removes that row from the edited schedule. Add Schedule notes only for information that applies to the whole schedule.

Check Public schedule preview and Next generated sessions carefully, including dates, times, cancellations and repeats. Review the Offering’s host Places, visibility and hide settings if those affect the programme.
Select Save Offering and wait for success. Reopen the Offering to verify the saved schedule; eligible sessions also feed Care Calendar, subject to the listing’s visibility and audience rules.
notes: If validation stops you, add at least one session, supply a valid start date/time, set any end after the start, choose at least one weekly repeat day, and ensure the first date matches a selected day. A last repeat date must not precede the first session. Remove or correct duplicate rows.

Older public schedule text remains until reviewed session rows are published. Publishing those rows replaces the older text with one generated schedule for the Offering and Care Calendar; check the generated preview before saving.
Saving a changed schedule alerts affected users inside CareAround to review their personal plans. It does not send email or WhatsApp, register anyone, create a provider booking or cancel a booking.

If another manager changed the schedule while you were saving, refresh the Offering, review the latest sessions and apply the intended changes again. Do not assume a failed save published your version.
A standard Offering linked to multiple Places uses one shared structured schedule. For different host-specific timing, review separate listings or the template/place-version workflow.

Edit place version uses a Local Schedule text field instead of this structured editor. A Resource Group also uses a separate Group form. Do not apply these Publish sessions instructions to those forms or promise Care Calendar entries from local schedule text.

When using the Guide’s supported new Programme/service draft, open Dates & recurrence and select Add dated sessions for Care Calendar. Requested timing text alone does not create sessions. Review the dates, then choose Review programme/service and explicitly Create programme/service; the Guide cannot update an existing schedule.

sections.title: Cancel a session or unpublish a Programme’s reviewed sessions
paragraphs: First confirm with the provider whether one date is cancelled, a whole recurring series is cancelled, or the published schedule should be withdrawn. These changes affect CareAround’s information and personal plans; they do not cancel a provider booking.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Offerings, select Edit on the exact Programme/service you may edit, and open Schedule.

For an individual session row that is cancelled, change Status to Cancelled and review the preview. Changing Status on a Recurring weekly row applies to that series; these controls do not establish cancellation of just one occurrence inside a weekly series.
To withdraw the reviewed sessions, turn off Publish sessions. If sessions were already published, read the Unpublish sessions? confirmation and its consequences.

Choose Unpublish sessions only if that is the intended change. Cancelling that confirmation leaves the switch unchanged. After confirming, review the form and select Save Offering to save the withdrawal.

Wait for a successful save and reopen the Offering to check its schedule. A status change likewise needs Save Offering. If the save fails or conflicts with a newer revision, refresh and review the current schedule before trying again.
notes: Unpublishing removes upcoming sessions from the Offering and Care Calendar. People with personal plans need to review the schedule change; the previous published version remains in schedule history.
Remove edits the session rows in this form; it is not a provider booking-cancellation control. Review the generated schedule before saving any removed rows.

If sessions have not yet been published, there is no previously published schedule to withdraw. If the Offering still shows older schedule text, publishing reviewed session rows is the separate replacement workflow described above.
A hidden Offering and an unpublished schedule are different things. Use the related visibility article when the intended change is to hide the listing rather than alter its dates.
The Guide cannot change an existing Offering or its schedule in chat. Use the exact listing’s edit form, and contact the provider separately about anyone’s registration or booking.

sections.title: Change an Offering’s published sessions
paragraphs: Open Manage My Resources → Offerings and choose Edit on a Programme/service you may edit. In Schedule, review the dated sessions or recurring weekly series and the public preview before saving. Turning off already published sessions asks for confirmation because upcoming sessions will leave the Offering and Care Calendar; people with personal plans must review the change. A changed schedule is not a provider booking cancellation, and the Guide cannot edit the existing Offering for you.

articles.title: Change resource visibility and distinguish hiding from deleting
articles.summary: Distinguish visibility changes, personal saved entries and permanent deletion.

sections.title: Hide or show one managed public listing
paragraphs: Use this flow only when the selected resource’s card offers the relevant visibility control. Visibility permission and editing permission are checked separately.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources and choose Places, Offerings or Groups. Find the exact listing and check its current hidden status.
Select Hide from app to hide it, or Show in app to restore it, when that control is offered. This card action starts the update immediately; it is not a Delete action.
Wait for the result, then check the refreshed card and intended visibility. If it fails, read the error and verify the listing’s permission before retrying.
notes: Showing a listing does not override its audience, linked-member or eligibility rules. A scheduled hide window may also affect whether it is currently visible.

Existing saved entries in My Directory are not automatically removed by hiding. They can remain unavailable for viewers who no longer have visibility, and become available again when visibility permits.
A heart or an Unsave action changes your saved collection. It does not hide or delete the public resource.
The Guide cannot change an existing listing’s visibility in chat.

sections.title: Set a planned hide window in a resource editor
paragraphs: Use the exact resource editor only if your account can change its visibility. A planned hide window is different from cancelling a Programme session or deleting the listing.
steps: Open Manage My Resources, choose the exact Place or Offering and select Edit if available.
For a Place, open Visibility. For a standard Offering, open Schedule and find Hide window.
Review Hide from App and enter the intended Scheduled Hide (From) and Scheduled Hide (Until) dates and times. Check that the values describe the intended period.
Review the public Preview and other audience rules, then choose Save Place or Save Offering as appropriate.
Wait for a successful save and reopen the exact resource to confirm its hide settings.
notes: A template-generated version has its own local Hide from app and scheduled hide controls; review that exact version rather than changing the shared template to unhide it.
If the form or card does not permit a visibility change, ask the responsible resource Owner or administrator. These instructions do not grant a wider scope.
If the intention is to withdraw dated sessions, use the schedules article. Hiding the listing is a different change.

sections.title: Confirm a visibility change for all filtered results
paragraphs: Bulk visibility controls apply across every page of the active filtered result set, not only the cards on screen. Review the complete scope before confirming.
steps: Open Manage My Resources and choose the relevant Places, Offerings or Groups tab. Set the intended search and Region filters.
Under Bulk actions for filtered results, select Hide all or Unhide all when available.
Read the confirmation’s resource count and filter details, including any results skipped because this account cannot change their visibility.
Choose Cancel if the scope is wrong. Otherwise explicitly select Hide all or Unhide all in the confirmation.
Wait for completion and review the result notice, including any partial failures. Check the affected listings before repeating an action.
notes: Resources already in the requested state remain unchanged. Permission checks still apply to each listing, and some results can be skipped.
Templates do not use these bulk listing controls. Save all and Unsave all concern your saved collection rather than public visibility.
An error or partial result is not evidence that every filtered resource changed; review the reported outcome.

sections.title: Review and confirm deletion of an exact listing
paragraphs: Delete is separate from Hide/Show and from removing a saved entry. Use it only when permanently removing the selected listing is intended and your account has the required permission.
steps: Open Manage My Resources and find the exact Place, Offering or Group. Confirm that its Delete control refers to the intended listing.
Before deleting a Place, review any linked Offerings and whether any rely solely on it. If you only need temporary removal from discovery, use Hide from app instead.
Select Delete and read the resource-specific confirmation. Choose Cancel if you selected the wrong listing or have not reviewed its dependencies.
Select Delete in the confirmation only when removal is intended, then wait for the result.
Check the refreshed resource list. If deletion fails, review the error and current state rather than assuming removal happened.
notes: The UI does not offer an undo for a deleted listing. Do not promise that the Guide can restore it.
Deleting an Offering template is a broader operation that also deletes its generated place versions; use the template article’s review steps.
Removing your own saved entry does not delete the public listing. The Guide cannot delete an existing listing for you.

sections.title: Hiding a public listing and existing saved entries
paragraphs: Hiding a public Place or Programme/service does not automatically remove people’s saved entries from My Directory. The saved entry can remain and be marked unavailable when that viewer can no longer see the listing. If the listing becomes visible to that viewer again, the same saved entry can become available again; other audience rules still apply. Hide/Show changes visibility and is separate from Delete. Removing your own saved entry is another action and does not delete the public listing. The Guide cannot inspect everybody’s saved list or confirm a particular person’s entry from this general question.

sections.title: Hide, show or delete a managed resource
paragraphs: In Manage My Resources, Hide from app or Show in app changes a Place or Offering’s visibility when that card permits it; it is separate from Delete. The filtered Hide all and Unhide all controls show a count-and-filter confirmation and skip items this account cannot change. Delete has its own confirmation and removes the listing from the directory; the UI does not offer an undo. Check the exact resource and any linked Offerings before deleting a Place. Saving or unsaving in My Directory does neither of these things.

sections.title: Directory visibility and Resource Claims approval
paragraphs: The ordinary Place or Offering editor has its own directory visibility controls and permission checks. Resource Claims publication approval is a separate governed-pilot workflow: after Owner verification and an active agreement, a Super Admin can approve selected provider fields and public uses in personal Shared Maps or embeds. That approval is not the general create step for every Discover listing, and the governed-pilot workspace may be unavailable in the current app release. The Guide cannot approve a claim or publish an existing listing from chat.

articles.title: Use Offering templates and place versions
articles.summary: Review shared template content and separate local place-version controls.

sections.title: Create a template, then generate hidden place versions
paragraphs: An Offering template holds shared Programme/service content. It is not itself a public listing. Use this workflow only if your account has the required template and host permissions.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources → Templates and select New Template if available.
In Profile, enter the template name, bucket, category, description and approved public website/contact details. Leave the optional External Key blank unless an approved workbook process requires one.
Open Defaults and review Default Schedule. In Visibility, review Audience, For linked members, Target areas where applicable and eligibility rules.
Review Generate: this step explains the next action but does not generate versions inside the unsaved form. Select Preview, check the shared content, then choose Create Template.
After the successful save, find the saved template and select Generate place versions.
Choose the intended Places in Eligible Hosts and check Generation Preview. Review which pairs already exist and which will become new hidden place versions.
Select Generate place versions and review the result. Existing active template/host pairs are skipped rather than duplicated.
Open Manage place versions, review each new host’s local details and visibility, and prepare that exact version before using its permitted Show in app or local visibility controls.
notes: Each generated version is tied to one host Place and starts hidden. Saving or editing the template does not automatically unhide those versions.

Shared fields come from the template; local schedule/contact overrides, availability and hidden status belong to the individual version. See the Programme/service article for Edit place version steps.
Default Schedule and a child’s Local Schedule are text fields in this workflow; do not promise structured Care Calendar sessions merely from entering text.
If New Template, a host or a generation action is unavailable, ask the responsible resource manager to review the exact permission. The server checks the template and each host.
The Guide cannot create a template or generate a batch of place versions in chat. Use only approved public content and keep private operating notes in the permitted restricted-content tools.

sections.title: Review propagation before saving a shared template change
paragraphs: A template edit can affect several active generated versions. Review the intended shared change and local overrides before saving.
steps: Open Manage My Resources → Templates and find the exact template you may manage.
Select Manage place versions to review the existing hosts and versions. Identify which values must remain host-specific.
Select Edit Template and change only the intended shared profile, defaults or visibility fields.
Select Preview, check the revised shared content, then choose Save Template.
Wait for success and review the affected versions. Use Edit place version for local details rather than broad template edits.
notes: Shared fields propagate to active versions unless that field has a local override. Local visibility and availability remain local controls; editing the template does not automatically publish a hidden version.
If a generated version must change its name or shared description, those fields are inherited and read-only in the local-version editor.
Reset on a local override immediately saves the removal and reloads its inherited value. Do not use it only as a preview or assume Cancel reverses it.
If the save fails, review the latest template and reported error before trying again. The Guide cannot edit either template or version in chat.

sections.title: Distinguish deleting a template from deleting one place version
paragraphs: Deleting a template also deletes all of its generated place versions. Review this wider consequence before selecting its Delete control.
steps: Open Manage My Resources → Templates and find the exact template.
Select Manage place versions and review every generated version before a whole-template deletion.
If the intention is to remove only one version, use that exact version’s permitted Delete control instead of the parent template’s Delete.
Select the intended Delete control, read its confirmation and choose Cancel if the target or consequence is wrong.
Explicitly confirm Delete only when intended, wait for the result, then check the refreshed template/version list.
notes: The reviewed UI has no restore workflow to promise. The Guide cannot delete or restore a template or version for you.
To temporarily take a version off discovery, review its local Hide from app control instead of deleting it.
If Delete is unavailable or the operation fails, request review of the exact template/version permission.

sections.title: Offering templates and place versions
paragraphs: An Offering template is shared Programme/service content, not itself a public listing. If New Template is available to your account, open Manage My Resources → Templates, choose New Template, review Profile, Defaults, Visibility, Generate and Translate, then choose Create Template. Save the template before choosing Generate place versions for selected host Places. The server checks permission for the template and every host; each newly generated place version starts hidden until its local details and visibility are reviewed. An existing active version at a selected host is skipped. The Guide’s direct Create action is for one new Programme/service, not a template or batch of place versions.

sections.title: Edit an Offering template and its place versions
paragraphs: An Offering template holds shared content for its generated place versions. When an authorised person saves a template edit, shared fields are propagated to existing active versions unless a field has a local override. A place version can keep its own schedule or contact overrides; its visibility and availability are local controls. Review the affected versions before saving a broad change, and use Edit place version for local details. Editing the template does not automatically unhide or publish a hidden version. The Guide cannot edit either one in chat.

sections.title: Delete an Offering template
paragraphs: Deleting an Offering template also deletes all of its generated place versions. In Manage My Resources → Templates, review the template and its place versions before using that template’s Delete control and confirmation. If you mean removing only one place version, open Manage place versions and choose that version instead. There is no reviewed restore workflow to promise from chat. The Guide cannot delete either one for you; the server checks the exact template or place-version permission.

articles.title: Create or manage public Resource Groups
articles.summary: Maintain a public collection without changing its member listings’ ownership.

sections.title: Create a Resource Group of existing public listings
paragraphs: A Resource Group is a directory collection of eligible public Places and Offerings. People belong in its separate Owner/Staff access controls, not as the collection’s resource members. Use New Group only when your account has the required permission.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources and select New Group if available.
In Profile, enter Group name, choose Category and add a public description and approved public contact/website details.
Open Visibility and review Who can see this? Choose Public or Target region/s. For Target region/s, search and select the intended existing Regions. Review Hide from public Discover.
Open Access and review Group Owner / Staff. Ensure at least one eligible account has Role → Owner; use Add access only for the intended additional operators.
Open Members, use Search places and offerings, and select the intended eligible public resource results. Check the selected member list and its readiness indication.
Select Preview and review the collection, audience, owner and members. Correct anything wrong, then select Save Group.
Wait for success and check the saved Group. A Group without an Owner or eligible public members is not ready for Discover.
notes: Adding another provider’s eligible public listing does not transfer its ownership or grant permission to edit that member listing.
Members must be eligible public, non-hidden resources. If no members are available, check the resource’s visibility and the loading/error message rather than adding private or hidden records.
Target region/s limits where the Group is shown, not a staff role. This editor has no staff-only audience, and Group membership does not change the visibility of the member listings.
An Org Group or Region Group of people is a separate coordination workflow. Do not create a public Resource Group as a substitute for a private staff group.
If New Group or an Owner account is unavailable, ask an authorised resource administrator to review the exact permission. The Guide cannot create Groups in chat.

sections.title: Edit a Resource Group’s details, audience or resource members
paragraphs: You need permission to edit the exact Group. Managing a member listing or having coordination-group membership does not by itself grant this Group’s editing rights.
steps: Open Manage My Resources → Groups and choose Edit on the exact Group if available.
Review Profile and Visibility. Keep only approved public details and choose the intended Public or Target region/s audience.
Open Members and review the selected Places/Offerings. Search eligible public resources to add a member, or remove a selected member when intended.
Select Preview and check the resulting collection, audience and visibility, then select Save Group.
Wait for the update and reopen the Group to verify it. If a save fails, review its error and current members before trying again.
notes: Editing the Group’s selected members does not edit or delete the member resources themselves and does not transfer their ownership.
The saved Group’s Access panel uses its separate permission-checked Add access and Remove actions. These actions save independently of profile edits.
If the intention is to hide or delete the collection, use the related visibility article. Do not use a public Group Delete control to archive a governance coordination group.
No staff-only audience is offered in this public Resource Group editor. The Guide cannot edit the collection or its members for you.

sections.title: Resource Groups
paragraphs: A Resource Group collects existing public Places and offerings, such as Programmes and services, into one directory collection. A governance coordination group is a different kind of group; membership there does not by itself grant editing rights to a resource.

sections.title: Create a Resource Group
paragraphs: If New Group is available to your account, open Manage My Resources and choose New Group. Give the Group a name, choose its audience and owner, select existing public Places or offerings as members, review the preview, then save. A Group without an owner or public members is not ready for Discover. This is a Resource Group, not a governance coordination group; your account and selected scope are checked when saving.

sections.title: Edit a Resource Group
paragraphs: Open Manage My Resources and choose Groups. On a Group you are allowed to edit, choose Edit to change its details or selected members, review the updated preview, then save. Members must be eligible public, non-hidden resources. If Edit is not shown for that Group, this Guide cannot grant access. Changes to a governance coordination group use a separate workflow.

sections.title: Another provider’s listing in a Resource Group
paragraphs: A Resource Group can include an eligible public, non-hidden Place or Offering from another provider. Adding that listing to a Group does not transfer its ownership or give the Group manager permission to edit the member listing. You still need permission to edit the Group itself; check the exact Group in Manage My Resources before changing its members.

sections.title: Target Regions for a Resource Group
paragraphs: In a Resource Group’s Visibility step, choose Public for everyone or Target region/s and select existing Regions. A target-region Group is shown only when the viewer is inside a selected Region boundary. The selected scope and your permission to change that Group are checked when saving; this does not change the visibility or ownership of its member listings.

sections.title: Resource Group staff-only visibility boundary
paragraphs: The current Resource Group Visibility step offers Public or Target region/s, not a staff-only audience. Target Regions limit where a Group is shown, not which staff role can view it. I cannot make a public Resource Group staff-only. If you mean a governance Org Group of people, that is a separate workflow.

sections.title: Resource Groups and coordination groups are separate
paragraphs: A public Resource Group collects existing eligible Places and Programmes/services as members; people are not added as its members. Org Groups and Region Groups are separate governance coordination groups, with separately checked access. The Guide cannot create either Group or add people in chat.

sections.title: The Guide does not archive a coordination group
paragraphs: A governance group has an Archived status, but the Guide cannot archive it in chat or verify that its members will remain visible after that change. Ask for your own current access check before opening the relevant permitted workspace.

articles.title: Review translations and preserve approved wording
articles.summary: Review translated wording while preserving English and staff-reviewed versions.

sections.title: Review and save translated wording for a managed resource
paragraphs: You must be able to edit the exact resource. English is the main version. Save the English public content first so the translation review compares against the current saved source.
steps: Open Dashboard → Manage My Resources and select Edit on the exact Place or Offering. For a template, use Edit Template on that saved template.
Open Translate. If the editor says to save the resource first, complete the English save, reopen the saved resource and return to Translate.
Choose the language card you want to review. Read its status and the fields needing attention alongside the displayed English wording.
If translated text is missing, use Fill all missing text or Refresh this language as appropriate, then review the generated wording rather than accepting it unseen.
Use Show all translated fields when you need to check or adjust fields that are currently hidden because they are ready.
Correct the visible translated text against the English meaning. Check names, instructions and sensitive wording carefully.
Select Save review and wait for the saved-review notice. Repeat for other languages that need review.
Reopen the review or the permitted public-language view to check the saved wording. If an action fails, review the error and current source before retrying.
notes: Saving unchanged automatically prepared text marks it reviewed. Changing the wording marks it staff edited, and staff-edited wording is not overwritten automatically when English changes.
Save review is a separate saved operation from Save Place, Save Offering or Save Template. Switching languages or closing an unsaved review does not submit edited text.
Refresh/fill actions respect protected staff-edited wording; do not promise a force-overwrite control. Review any retained wording after the English source changes.
Use the correct template or place-version editor for inherited versus local fields. Do not infer that translating a shared template and translating a local override are the same operation.
The Guide cannot translate or save edits to an existing resource in chat. Keep private operating information out of public-language fields.

sections.title: Translate a managed Programme/service
paragraphs: The Guide cannot translate or edit an existing Programme/service in chat. If Edit is available on the exact listing, open Manage My Resources → Offerings → Edit → Translate. Save its English content first, then review the language cards. The editor can fill missing translated text or refresh one language; check the wording and choose Save review. English remains the main version, and staff-edited wording is not overwritten automatically. The server checks permission for the selected listing.
